item.title: Steelers Get Telling Trade Deadline Explanation From ESPN Insider
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - NOVEMBER 01: Aaron Rodgers #8 of the Pittsburgh Steelers passes the ball during the second quarter against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on November 01, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers had an opportunity to add to a 6-2 team at the NFL trade deadline. General manager Omar Khan instead kept his draft picks, and a new report points to a bigger decision awaiting the franchise. While other AFC contenders made moves, Pittsburgh stood pat despite questions at wide receiver and in the secondary. According to ESPN, the Steelers’ approach has plenty to do with what happens after Aaron Rodgers. ESPN Reveals Steelers’ Trade Deadline Reasoning ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reported that Pittsburgh was one of only two AFC teams with at least six wins that failed to make a trade before Tuesday’s deadline. The Cincinnati Bengals were the other, although they reportedly backed out of a deal. Pryor pointed directly to the franchise’s unsettled quarterback future. “PIT has maintained that it doesn’t want to give up significant draft capital until it has a clear future QB plan,” Pryor wrote. That position matches what Pryor wrote in an earlier ESPN deadline preview . “Don’t mortgage the future for the present,” Pryor wrote, later adding that Pittsburgh’s “top priority remains finding their next franchise quarterback.” Rodgers, 42, has said this will be his final NFL season. The Steelers have Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar behind him, but haven’t settled on a successor. Khan expressed optimism about the younger quarterbacks earlier this season. “We’re excited about the future with those guys, so glad we have them,” he said, according to Steelers.com’s Brian Batko . Steelers Pass on Josh Downs and Other Receivers Pittsburgh’s decision was especially noticeable at wide receiver. Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reported that the Steelers explored trades for Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs, Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Tennessee Titans receiver Calvin Ridley. Downs ended up with the Kansas City Chiefs , who sent Indianapolis 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks and received a seventh-rounder along with the receiver. Pittsburgh no longer owns its 2027 fourth-round pick, having sent it to Dallas in a deal the Steelers announced in August. That deal brought back third- and sixth-round selections, leaving the Steelers with two picks in the third round. Thomas and Ridley remained with their teams. The Steelers’ need wasn’t imagined. Michael Pittman Jr. has played just three games because of a foot injury, while Roman Wilson has been out with a hand injury. Coach Mike McCarthy said Pittman is “getting close” to returning, according to an Associated Press report by Will Graves . Wilson could return later this month. (Photo by Justin K. Aller/Getty Images) Getty The Pittsburgh Steelers had an opportunity to add to a 6-2 team at the NFL trade deadline. General manager Omar Khan instead kept his draft picks, and a new report points to a bigger decision awaiting the franchise. While other AFC contenders made moves, Pittsburgh stood pat despite questions at wide receiver and in the secondary. According to ESPN, the Steelers’ approach has plenty to do with what happens after Aaron Rodgers. ESPN Reveals Steelers’ Trade Deadline Reasoning ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reported that Pittsburgh was one of only two AFC teams with at least six wins that failed to make a trade before Tuesday’s deadline. The Cincinnati Bengals were the other, although they reportedly backed out of a deal. Pryor pointed directly to the franchise’s unsettled quarterback future. “PIT has maintained that it doesn’t want to give up significant draft capital until it has a clear future QB plan,” Pryor wrote. That position matches what Pryor wrote in an earlier ESPN deadline preview . “Don’t mortgage the future for the present,” Pryor wrote, later adding that Pittsburgh’s “top priority remains finding their next franchise quarterback.” Rodgers, 42, has said this will be his final NFL season. The Steelers have Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and rookie Drew Allar behind him, but haven’t settled on a successor. Khan expressed optimism about the younger quarterbacks earlier this season. “We’re excited about the future with those guys, so glad we have them,” he said, according to Steelers.com’s Brian Batko . Steelers Pass on Josh Downs and Other Receivers Pittsburgh’s decision was especially noticeable at wide receiver. Pittsburgh Post-Gazette’s Gerry Dulac reported that the Steelers explored trades for Indianapolis Colts receiver Josh Downs, Jacksonville Jaguars receiver Brian Thomas Jr. and Tennessee Titans receiver Calvin Ridley. Downs ended up with the Kansas City Chiefs , who sent Indianapolis 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks and received a seventh-rounder along with the receiver. Pittsburgh no longer owns its 2027 fourth-round pick, having sent it to Dallas in a deal the Steelers announced in August. That deal brought back third- and sixth-round selections, leaving the Steelers with two picks in the third round. Thomas and Ridley remained with their teams. The Steelers’ need wasn’t imagined. Michael Pittman Jr. has played just three games because of a foot injury, while Roman Wilson has been out with a hand injury. Coach Mike McCarthy said Pittman is “getting close” to returning, according to an Associated Press report by Will Graves . Wilson could return later this month. Pittsburgh is counting on reinforcements already under contract rather than another trade. Steelers’ QB Future Remains a Bigger Question Khan took a similar approach last year, passing on receivers while preserving picks that could help Pittsburgh move up for a quarterback. Pittsburgh eventually added veteran help during the season, but its offense struggled in a playoff loss to Houston. There’s a possible cost to repeating that approach. The Steelers have won four straight and lead the AFC North, yet they’re entering the second half without the receiver addition that other contenders pursued. Still, preserving draft capital gives Khan more flexibility next spring. Pittsburgh already acquired another 2027 third-rounder from Dallas, and its first-round selection remains available if it decides to pursue a quarterback in the draft. For now, Mike McCarthy will have to make the playoff push with Rodgers and the receivers already on the roster. Pittsburgh protected its picks at the deadline, but that puts even more importance on getting its next quarterback decision right. item.title: Ryan Friedkin to arrive in Rome for transfer summit
item.description: Ryan Friedkin to arrive in Rome for transfer summit The main question Roma fans have been asking themselves in the last few hours is clear: how far can Gasperini’s team go with a major signing in the January transfer window? For some, the answer is simple: they can win the Scudetto. This question is fueling the thoughts of Gasperini and the Giallorossi management, starting with Tony D’Amico, who will be extremely busy meeting the manager’s demands. They’re also waiting for a signal from the Friedkins. In the coming weeks, the American ownership will be grappling with the final decisive steps for the stadium in Pietralata, UEFA’s ruling on the settlement agreement, and the January transfer window itself. Gasperini’s mission to strengthen Roma through the January transfer window will involve the Friedkins. As reported by Corriere dello Sport , Ryan Friedkin is expected in the capital in the coming days to discuss strategies for the upcoming transfer campaign. A plane is ready to take off from Houston, but it’s not out of the question that it could be carrying Corbin Friedkin. The ownership’s presence in Trigoria means they’re ready to go. Gasperini doesn’t want to waste time and needs a complete squad to maintain the team’s competitiveness.

item.title: Ravens Deadline Move All About Securing Depth
item.description: ATLANTA, GEORGIA - JANUARY 08: Desmond Ridder #4 of the Atlanta Falcons talks with Ryan Neuzil #64 prior to the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on January 08, 2023 in Atlanta, Georgia. (Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) Getty The Baltimore Ravens were active during Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. The Ravens secured C Ryan Neuzil from the Atlanta Falcons for G Andrew Vorhees and a sixth-round pick in the 2028 NFL Draft. The move might seem like an under-the-radar acquisition. But for Baltimore, the move screams depth. The team has already lost three centers this season. The losses of Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn, and Ethan Pocic forced the organization to acquire a replacement from the Philadelphia Eagles in Cam Jurgens. Now, Jurgens has been in this for three games. But the problem is that should Jurgens go down, or really any other lineman, the situation could leave the Ravens in a pickle. That’s why this deal makes sense. And as Daniel Popper noted in The Athletic , Neuzil offers depth, but also flexibility should anyone else go down this season. “Neuzil has been solid for the Falcons this season, and he is a fit in offensive coordinator Declan Doyle’s scheme. Standout rookie guard Vega Ioane was dealing with a knee sprain, but he returned in Week 9. Perhaps the Ravens wanted to shore up their center depth? They now have a capable answer if Jurgens gets injured. Or they can move Jurgens to guard if one of the guards, Ioane or John Simpson, suffers an injury. Vorhees did not play well in two starts this season. Having Neuzil would help prevent the Ravens from having to move Ioane back to center, which they did in an emergency earlier this year.” Popper gave the Ravens a B- for the deal. It’s not a bad bit of business, considering the circumstances. Ravens Still Have a Playoff Shot, and They Know It At 4-5, the Ravens don’t have much runway, but their playoff hopes are not exactly on life support. Baltimore still has the playoffs within reach. That’s why throwing in the towel now doesn’t make any sense. And if the organization thinks that it has a legit chance to challenge for the Super Bowl, it needs to take steps to avoid devastating issues. Hence, the offensive line is an obvious concern. Baltimore has already dealt with a revolving door at center, and another injury could leave the club in a pretty pickle. It’s also worth noting that Jurgens has only been with the team for three games, that’s why having another capable option behind him makes sense. The Ravens also need to protect their flexibility at guard rather than constantly reshuffling the line whenever someone goes down. That’s what makes Ryan Neuzil a sensible addition. Make no mistake. This isn’t a move that will suddenly transform Baltimore’s offense. But it’s the type of move that could prevent one more injury from becoming a devastating problem. At this point, the Ravens need every bit of stability they can find. If they want to stay in the playoff hunt

(Photo by Alex Slitz/Getty Images) Getty The Baltimore Ravens were active during Tuesday’s NFL trade deadline. The Ravens secured C Ryan Neuzil from the Atlanta Falcons for G Andrew Vorhees and a sixth-round pick in the 2028 NFL Draft. The move might seem like an under-the-radar acquisition. But for Baltimore, the move screams depth. The team has already lost three centers this season. The losses of Danny Pinter, Jovaughn Gwyn, and Ethan Pocic forced the organization to acquire a replacement from the Philadelphia Eagles in Cam Jurgens. Now, Jurgens has been in this for three games. But the problem is that should Jurgens go down, or really any other lineman, the situation could leave the Ravens in a pickle. That’s why this deal makes sense. And as Daniel Popper noted in The Athletic , Neuzil offers depth, but also flexibility should anyone else go down this season. “Neuzil has been solid for the Falcons this season, and he is a fit in offensive coordinator Declan Doyle’s scheme. Standout rookie guard Vega Ioane was dealing with a knee sprain, but he returned in Week 9. Perhaps the Ravens wanted to shore up their center depth? They now have a capable answer if Jurgens gets injured. Or they can move Jurgens to guard if one of the guards, Ioane or John Simpson, suffers an injury. Vorhees did not play well in two starts this season. Having Neuzil would help prevent the Ravens from having to move Ioane back to center, which they did in an emergency earlier this year.” Popper gave the Ravens a B- for the deal. It’s not a bad bit of business, considering the circumstances. Ravens Still Have a Playoff Shot, and They Know It At 4-5, the Ravens don’t have much runway, but their playoff hopes are not exactly on life support. Baltimore still has the playoffs within reach. That’s why throwing in the towel now doesn’t make any sense. And if the organization thinks that it has a legit chance to challenge for the Super Bowl, it needs to take steps to avoid devastating issues. Hence, the offensive line is an obvious concern. Baltimore has already dealt with a revolving door at center, and another injury could leave the club in a pretty pickle. The Ravens also need to protect their flexibility at guard rather than constantly reshuffling the line whenever someone goes down. That’s what makes Ryan Neuzil a sensible addition. Make no mistake. This isn’t a move that will suddenly transform Baltimore’s offense. But it’s the type of move that could prevent one more injury from becoming a devastating problem. At this point, the Ravens need every bit of stability they can find. If they want to stay in the playoff hunt, shoring up the offensive line is a pretty good place to start. Baltimore Got Neuzil for a Reasonable Price The other appealing part of this deal is what Baltimore actually had to give up to get Neuzil. The Falcons could have taken Baltimore to the cleaners. The Ravens’ need was clear, and it could have given Atlanta a chance to clean up. Instead, the Falcons actually did Baltimore a solid. Instead of sticking it to them, Atlanta was willing to take a much lower return than it could have otherwise gotten. What Baltimore paid was a relatively modest price for a player who gives Baltimore another legitimate option across the interior offensive line. Vorhees had struggled in his opportunities this season, making the cost easier to stomach. And while giving up a draft pick is never ideal, a late-round selection two years from now is a small price to pay for insurance at a position that has already caused the team plenty of headaches. The Ravens didn’t need to make a splash at the deadline. They needed to address a weakness before it became an even bigger problem. item.title: Teddy Riner candidacy 'illustrative of this hunger for an alternative' to Le Pen or Mélenchon
item.description: As Teddy Riner throws his hat in the race for the French presidency, amid France's sociopolitical and economic crises, François Picard is pleased to welcome Lex Paulson, Director of Executive Programs at UM6P School of Collective Intelligence at at Mohammed VI Polytechnic University. The prospect of Olympic judo champion Teddy Riner entering France's presidential race raises questions that extend well beyond the political ambitions of a celebrated and beloved athlete. At a time when traditional parties are struggling to mobilize voters and the political center remains deeply fragmented, Riner's emergence points to a broader transformation of French politics weathering multiple crises: the growing importance of personal credibility, public visibility and the capacity to embody an alternative to established political elites.
item.dc:creator: François PICARD

item.title: Kings’ Darius Acuff Jr. doesn’t hold back on 1-10 record after loss to Magic
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Sergio Estrada-Imagn Images Kings’ Darius Acuff Jr. doesn’t hold back on 1-10 record after loss to Magic appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Sacramento Kings are spiraling early in the season, and rookie point guard Darius Acuff Jr. isn’t trying to sugarcoat the frustration anymore. Sacramento hit another low point on Tuesday night, falling 107-100 to the Orlando Magic at Golden 1 Center. The defeat dropped the Kings to a dismal 1-10 record, tying the worst 11-game start in franchise history. Despite the team’s ongoing slide, Acuff put on another spectacular individual show. The 18-year-old guard led Sacramento’s attack with 29 points, six assists, and four rebounds while playing 40 minutes. But personal box-score numbers meant very little to the rookie after watching another winnable game slip away in front of the home crowd. Following the loss, beat reporter Frankie Cartoscelli posted on X that Acuff was visibly frustrated while addressing the media. The rookie guard held nothing back when assessing Sacramento’s struggles. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “1-10 just don’t sound right,” Acuff said. “There’s nobody to blame but ourselves… We’re trying; we’re talking as a team. When the clock hits zero and we’re losing, that’s the most frustrating part.”Acuff has shouldered a massive load early, becoming the first NBA rookie since 1983 to attempt at least 20 shots in each of his first 10 career games. He got offensive support from veteran guard Zach LaVine, but Sacramento couldn’t string together enough late stops. Orlando executed key possessions down the stretch, keeping the Kings winless at home with an 0-6 mark. Sacramento’s locker room communication has yet to pay dividends on the court. While Acuff continues to show superstar potential, high-scoring nights won’t soften the blow for a rookie driven by winning. Until the Kings fix their late-game execution, the frustration in Sacramento will only build. item.title: 76ers’ Joel Embiid calls Paul George Celtics’ ‘best player’
item.description: © Bill Streicher-Imagn Images 76ers’ Joel Embiid calls Paul George Celtics’ ‘best player’ appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Philadelphia 76ers star Joel Embiid is very happy for his former teammate and Celtics veteran, Paul George. In a 123-101 loss to the Celtics, foul trouble disrupted 76ers All-Star Jaylen Brown’s rhythm against his former team. At the same time, the other player involved in their blockbuster trade over the summer — George — thrived, scoring a game-high 36 points in his first game back in Philadelphia. While fans were fixated on how the former Celtic would perform against his former team, Brown might have had his worst game since his trade. George, on the other hand, turned in his best of the young regular season, of which Embiid commended during his postgame availability, per PHLY Sports’ Derek Bodner. “Off the court we have a special relationship. Families are close, especially our kids. I love him,” Embiid said. “That’s why I’m extremely happy for him. He’s healthy, he’s playing well. The start of the season, you see what he did tonight. You can kinda say he’s been their best player on some level. So, I’m extremely happy for him. Proud of him.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Joel Embiid on his relationship with Paul George : "Off the court we have a special relationship. Families are close, especially our kids. I love him. That's why I'm extremely happy for him. He's healthy, he's playing well…You can kinda say he's been their best player." pic.twitter.com/WCRUsrBO3d — Derek Bodner (@DerekBodnerNBA) November 11, 2026 Celtics’ Paul George drained six threes en route to his 36 points. He also finished with five rebounds and one assist, while Jayson Tatum tallied 21 points, six rebounds, four assists, and two blocks. 76ers’ Joel Embiid finished with 16 points, six rebounds, and one assist. Tyrese Maxey’s 24 points led Philly in scoring, while Brown added 13 points, five rebounds, two assists two steals, and one block against the Celtics. Embiid and the 76ers will look to bounce back from their 22-point loss when they host the Toronto Raptors on Thursday. Related: 76ers star Jaylen Brown’s simple NSFW reaction to poor play in revenge game vs. Celtics Related: 76ers HC Nick Nurse reveals why Jaylen Brown had ‘no chance to get going’ vs. Celtics

item.title: The Promise And The Proof
item.description: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. item.content:encoded: Tinubu is asking for time to complete his reforms. His challengers must explain how they would deliver better results. The most consequential promise from today’s campaign platform concerns something Nigerians can judge without a political analyst: whether the lights stay on. Speaking at the APC rally in Dutse, President Bola Tinubu promised reliable electricity, lower living costs, support for smaller businesses and more jobs if re-elected. These commitments reach directly into the daily calculations of households and enterprises. For the tailor buying fuel, the graduate searching for work and the family stretching its food budget, the question is immediate: how soon will improvement arrive? That question now sits at the centre of Tinubu’s re-election argument. The APC unveiled its second-term manifesto today, defending the administration’s reforms while promising improvements in security, living standards, infrastructure and governance. The campaign is asking Nigerians to connect the disruption of the present with the prospect of a more prosperous future. It is a politically demanding request. Voters must decide whether the government has established a credible foundation for improvement and whether their experience gives them sufficient reason to renew its mandate. A New Manifesto Meets An Existing Record An incumbent’s manifesto arrives with a companion document: the record of the government seeking another term. The APC’s new commitments include additional electricity meters, wider health insurance coverage and a reduction in the number of out-of-school children. Its presentation also promised identifiable delivery responsibilities and public reporting of progress. These are campaign commitments, whose implementation remains to be demonstrated. That creates an opportunity for a more useful election debate. On electricity, candidates should explain how proposed investments would improve supply to homes and businesses. On employment, they should distinguish training places, temporary opportunities and sustained paid work. On education, they should explain how children will enter school, remain there and learn. The opposition has a responsibility here too. Criticism of government performance becomes more persuasive when accompanied by a workable alternative. A promise to make life affordable needs an explanation of costs, funding and consequences. A promise to improve security needs an account of personnel, intelligence, accountability and protection for affected communities. The campaign can now be judged against specific proposals. Nigerians should expect the candidates to defend them. Rivers: Reconciliation Has Become an Electoral Asset Saturday’s Port Harcourt rally gave Tinubu something beyond a large political gathering: a public display of cooperation between Nyesom Wike and Governor Siminalayi Fubara. The President welcomed their reconciliation. Fubara pledged at least three million votes for Tinubu; an ambitious campaign undertaking that should be reported as a pledge, rather than an electoral projection. The strategic significance lies in organisation. Politicians who previously directed their energies against one another are presenting themselves as partners in the presidential campaign. If that cooperation extends through local structures, it could strengthen mobilisation. But agreement among leaders still has to survive competition over other offices, local grievances and differing expectations of political reward. Rivers also carries particular significance because Atiku Abubakar’s running mate, Rotimi Amaechi, is a former governor of the state. The presidential contest therefore intersects with an established struggle over political influence. The next evidence to examine is whether cooperation on the platform produces coordinated work across communities and polling units. Atiku’s Campaign Must Sustain Confidence For the ADC, the immediate challenge remains the legal uncertainty surrounding its leadership and nominations. The campaign says it has filed an appeal and an application for a stay of execution against the November 5 judgment, and notified INEC. Reporting on those filings stated that the stay application had not been determined; filing an appeal does not itself suspend the judgment. The reports reviewed for this edition do not establish a subsequent order granting that relief. The distinction matters because supporters need accurate information about the campaign they are being asked to sustain. Atiku’s camp continues to allege political interference. Those allegations require evidence and a response from the institutions concerned. They cannot substitute for an authoritative account of the court orders and subsequent proceedings. Politically, uncertainty creates practical pressures: organisers need direction, candidates need reassurance and resources must remain available. The ADC’s task is to pursue its legal challenge while keeping its economic and security proposals before voters. A campaign consumed by defending its participation risks losing opportunities to explain its purpose. Obi’s Benue Visit Will Test Campaign Access The NDC has announced that Peter Obi is scheduled to visit Yelwata and hold a town hall in Makurdi on Wednesday, November 11. Its Benue governorship candidate, Terhemba Shija, has alleged plans to disrupt the visit. A Benue government official has denied that allegation. The visit remains forthcoming. The immediate requirement is straightforward: lawful political activity should proceed safely. A visit to a community affected by violence also demands sensitivity. Bereaved and displaced families should have the space to explain their circumstances, with their dignity protected. For Obi, the policy test will be whether solidarity is accompanied by credible proposals for security, recovery and livelihoods. For the authorities, the test is equal protection. Political disagreement provides no justification for obstructing lawful access to citizens. Four Campaigns, Different Tests Tinubu and the APC: Today’s manifesto and Dutse rally strengthen the campaign’s focus on delivery. The challenge is to explain why a further term would resolve problems Nigerians continue to experience during the current one. Atiku and the ADC: The most consequential immediate development would be an authoritative appellate decision or a formal INEC action. Political defiance can sustain morale, but legal clarity remains essential. Obi and the NDC: Tomorrow’s announced Benue visit will test access, organisation and the ability to connect community concerns with national policy. Claims about expanding support need evidence beyond attendance and publicity. Seyi Makinde and the APM: Makinde unveiled his “Reset Nigeria” manifesto on November 4, outlining proposals on the economy, security, education and social development. His campaign’s test is whether it can turn those proposals into a recognisable national organisation and electoral constituency. The opposition remains distributed across competing platforms. That gives dissatisfied voters alternatives, while requiring each challenger to build sufficient breadth of support. There is no verified evidence in the developments reviewed to assign a fresh national lead or declare a decisive transfer of votes. State-level organisation deserves particular attention. Reconciliation, defections and endorsements matter when they change mobilisation and voting behaviour. Recent local and off-cycle contests can help assess those structures, provided turnout, competitiveness and local circumstances are considered. Put the Promises Through a Young Person’s Budget Today’s emphasis on electricity, enterprise and employment gives the Youth Metre a practical focus. Consider a young Nigerian trying to operate a small business. Reliable power could reduce costs. Affordable transport could widen access to customers and work. Effective training could improv

After spending two seasons with the Sixers, George produced averages of 16.7 points, while shooting 37.5% from three. He had some decent moments, like last year’s playoff series against the Boston Celtics in round one, but ultimately, the Paul George experience was a disappointment. The 76ers gladly traded the veteran forward to the Celtics, along with draft compensation in order to acquire Jaylen Brown. It was a celebrated trade on Philly’s side, and a controversial one in Boston. But so far, George is proving the doubters wrong, and got a sprinkle of revenge against the 76ers on Tuesday night in Philly. After the game, George stated the reason behind his re-emergence. The first two years I was here in Philly,” George said after the game . Over two seasons, George played in just 78 games. Being inconsistent with his availability, George couldn’t ramp up to his full potential. With the Celtics, he has been able to so far. “I’m a little bit better with more usage, and that’s no knock to my opportunities here with Philly. He had some decent moments, like last year’s playoff series against the Boston Celtics in round one, but ultimately, the Paul George experience was a disappointment. The 76ers gladly traded the veteran forward to the Celtics, along with draft compensation in order to acquire Jaylen Brown. It was a celebrated trade on Philly’s side, and a controversial one in Boston. But so far, George is proving the doubters wrong, and got a sprinkle of revenge against the 76ers on Tuesday night in Philly. After the game, George stated the reason behind his re-emergence. Paul George Reveals Reason Behind Turnaround After 76ers-Celtics Game Getty PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA – NOVEMBER 10: Paul George #13 of the Boston Celtics shoots the ball against Vj Edgecombe #77 of the Philadelphia 76ers in the third quarter at Xfinity Mobile Arena on November 10, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. The Celtics defeated the 76ers 123-101. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Mitchell Leff/Getty Images) When George was asked about the difference between his Philly stint and the first 10 games of his Boston stint, it boils down to one thing: being healthy. “That was the biggest challenge, the biggest hurdle. The first two years I was here in Philly,” George said after the game . Over two seasons, George played in just 78 games. Being inconsistent with his availability, George couldn’t ramp up to his full potential. With the Celtics, he has been able to so far. “I’m a little bit better with more usage, and that’s no knock to my opportunities here with Philly. Quite frankly, I wasn’t healthy to take on the workload that I feel I’m at my best at. But here in Boston, they gave me an opportunity to come out here and play and be myself. Joe has integrated me right into the offense and allowed me to just be myself.” Before Tuesday’s game, George was back on track with All-Star-level production. The veteran wing is producing 20.4 points per game, while shooting 42.5% from three at a high volume. In 30 minutes against the Sixers on Tuesday, George hit on six of his 11 shots from three, producing a total of 36 points. He helped lead the Celtics to a dominant 123-101 victory to move to 9-2 on the season. item.title: Colts headline 3 biggest losers of 2026 NFL trade deadline after keeping Jonathan Taylor
item.description: Colts headline 3 biggest losers of 2026 NFL trade deadline after keeping Jonathan Taylor appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . And just like that, the 2026 NFL trade deadline was in the books . Suddenly, all of the rumors were either proven true or false, all of the speculation came to an end, and fans had a chance to see what their favorites will more or less look like when the playoffs roll around come January. For some teams, they made out like bandits, adding the perfect players for their schemes at a reasonable price, but for others, three teams exactly, things didn’t go exactly how they’d hoped, leaving picks on the table, overpaying for players, or simply showing a fundamental misunderstanding of the rules that resulted in a major faux pas on deadline day. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mandatory Credit: Travis Register-Imagn Images The Colts left too many picks on the table by keeping Jonathan Taylor As an entire swash of NFL teams looked to load up on the finishing touches for their Super Bowl-caliber rosters, the Colts and Eagles found themselves as the two biggest sellers in a buyer’s market and were able to load up on draft picks in exchange for win-now players. And yet, when push came to shove, the Colts removed their best chip from the table before the die was cast, losing out on “ a second-round pick and more ” for 27-year-old running back Jonathan Taylor , according to Fox Sports’ Jordan Schutlz. “Sources: The Colts had multiple offers of a 2nd-round pick and more for RB Jonathan Taylor over the last week,” Schutlz wrote. “But the organization decided that if it ever trades him, it will be in the offseason, when more buyers could be available, and a permanent GM is in place.” On paper, the idea of waiting until the offseason to trade Taylor isn’t the worst one, as there could be additional teams interested in his services, but what there won’t be is the same sense of urgency that exists at the trade deadline, where teams are willing to pay extra for that missing piece. Factor in the potential for Taylor to get injured over the final eight games, where he’s averaging 20.7 touches per game, and the Colts are making a major bet that might not cash in the way they hope. The Colts also opted against trading Grover Stewart , who is a free agent at the end of the season, and probably could have gotten way more than a third-round pick for Daniel Jones from the Minnesota Vikings if they were willing to really sell the doors off their building, which may or may not pay off, depending on how the next 12 months shake out. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Mandatory Credit: Travis Register-Imagn Images The Colts left too many picks on the table by keeping Jonathan Taylor As an entire swash of NFL teams looked to load up on the finishing touches for their Super Bowl-caliber rosters, the Colts and Eagles found themselves as the two biggest sellers in a buyer’s market and were able to load up on draft picks in exchange for win-now players. And yet, when push came to shove, the Colts removed their best chip from the table before the die was cast, losing out on “ a second-round pick and more ” for 27-year-old running back Jonathan Taylor , according to Fox Sports’ Jordan Schutlz. “Sources: The Colts had multiple offers of a 2nd-round pick and more for RB Jonathan Taylor over the last week,” Schutlz wrote. “But the organization decided that if it ever trades him, it will be in the offseason, when more buyers could be available, and a permanent GM is in place.” On paper, the idea of waiting until the offseason to trade Taylor isn’t the worst one, as there could be additional teams interested in his services, but what there won’t be is the same sense of urgency that exists at the trade deadline, where teams are willing to pay extra for that missing piece. Factor in the potential for Taylor to get injured over the final eight games, where he’s averaging 20.7 touches per game, and the Colts are making a major bet that might not cash in the way they hope. The Colts also opted against trading Grover Stewart , who is a free agent at the end of the season, and probably could have gotten way more than a third-round pick for Daniel Jones from the Minnesota Vikings if they were willing to really sell the doors off their building, which may or may not pay off, depending on how the next 12 months shake out. Eric Hartline-Imagn Images The Jaguars were rightfully blasted for Jordan Davis ’ price tag On Monday, the Jacksonville Jaguars shocked the NFL world by not only trading for Jessie Bates III and Davon Godchaux but also backing up the Brinks truck to the deadline’s other big seller, the Eagles, to take over the remainder of Jordan Davis’ long-term contract. When the news broke, Jaguars fans were rightfully excited, as they nabbed a key defensive cog from a recent Super Bowl champion to hopefully lead them to their own run at the “big game,” but as the dust settled, it rapidly looked like Howie Roseman fleeced James Gladstone out of a 2027 first-round pick and a 2029 second-rounder for a part-time player in the middle of a down season. Need proof? Well, look no further than ESPN, where a tag team article by Ben Solak and Seth Walder gave the Jaguars an F for the deal. Why? Well, because Davis simply isn’t the kind of player worthy of that kind of return. “There’s no other way to start this: This trade is a disaster for Jacksonville,” the duo wrote. “The numbers do not paint a picture of Davis being someone who is worth anywhere near that type of trade compensation. He has played 52% of snaps for the Eagles. That number is not particularly unusual for a run-stuffing nose tackle, but that’s exactly the point: The Jaguars just dealt first- and second-round picks for a part-time player who helps only against the run! There is no world where that is worth it.” Now granted, Davis brings more to the table than just stopping the run. He’s a great locker room guy, a team leader, and one of the most athletic nose tackles the NFL has ever seen. But the Eagles simply never trusted him to rush the passer with regularity, which is a big part of playing defensive tackle in the NFL regardless of scheme, especially on a $78 million contract. Who knows, maybe the Jaguars will give Davis more of a go since they don’t also have Jalen Carter and Moro Ojomo looking for snaps, but unless he suddenly becomes a three-down player, it’s hard to argue the Jaguars didn’t pay a serious premium for a part-time player, which is all the more confusing since they added another run-stuffing defensive tackle earlier in the day. Edward Finan-Imagn Images The Bengals not knowing the compensatory draft formula rules Normally, when a team opts to trade a sixth-round pick for a rotational edge rusher, it’s pretty low on the proverbial priority list, especially when multiple first- and second-round picks were moved before the deadline. The Cincinnati Bengals ’ decision to almost trade for Eagles outside linebacker Arnold Ebiketie is the rare exception, as the reason it didn’t happen is downright goofy. Taking to social media to explain the situation for fans who don’t know the inner workings of the compensatory formula – a disproportionate number of whom may live in the Buckeye State – The Ringers’ Albert Breer revealed that had the deal gone through, Duke Tobin would have been giving up a whole lot more than a sixth-round pick . “Explaining the Arnold Ebiketie situation. The rule in question was put in years ago to close a loophole teams could exploit by executing a sign-and-trade with other teams—and basically says that if you trade for a player in the first year of his contract, he counts against the comp-pick formula as if he was a free agent you signed,” Breer wrote. “Had the Bengals gone through with this trade, they’d have gained three compensable free agents, and lost three, leaving them without a pick for Trey Hendrickson. So while on paper, they’d have gotten Ebiketie for a sixth-rounder, as a practical matter, they’d have traded him for third- and sixth-round picks (the third being the comp pick they’ll likely get for Hendrickson). That’s why the trade is off.” At the end of the day, does it really matter if the Bengals added a player like Ebiketie, who doesn’t have a sack in 2026 over 300 defensive snaps? Not really, especially since their pass rush currently ranks ninth in the NFL in terms of sacks, and players like Boye Mafe have come into their own without Trey Henderson. But not knowing how the compensatory pick formula works? Especially when Tobin has been with the team for 25 years? That certainly is not a good look for a team that has routinely been on the wrong side of personal drama. Related: Where 2026 NFL trade deadline falls in league history Related: Josh Downs trade grades for Chiefs, Colts as Patrick Mahomes gets new weapon

item.title: Liverpool prodigy Rio Ngumoha explains how Barcelona superstar has inspired young footballers: ‘He plays as if…’
item.description: Liverpool prodigy Rio Ngumoha explains how Barcelona superstar has inspired young footballers: ‘He plays as if…’ Liverpool youngster Rio Ngumoha has credited Barcelona forward Lamine Yamal with changing the way young footballers approach the game, describing the teenager as one of the best players in the world. Speaking in an interview with The Independent , the 18-year-old England international highlighted how Yamal’s confidence, freedom and performances at such a young age have inspired the next generation. Ngumoha’s comments come ahead of England’s November Nations League fixtures against Croatia and Spain. Thomas Tuchel has included the Liverpool winger in his squad following his encouraging performances at club level, potentially giving him an opportunity to face the Barcelona star when England meet Spain. Ngumoha sees Yamal as an inspiration for young players Speaking during a lengthy interview, Ngumoha did not hide his admiration when asked about the Barcelona winger, whose development has established him among the leading young talents in European football. Rio Ngumoha sees Lamine Yamal as an inspiration. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) “I think what he’s doing has changed football for young players. He’s extraordinary. He’s one of the best in the world,” said Ngumoha when asked about the Barcelona star. The Liverpool forward believes Yamal’s performances show that young footballers should not be afraid to express themselves or take responsibility on the pitch. Rather than allowing their age to restrict their ambitions, they can use his example as encouragement to play with confidence. “Seeing what he can do at such a young age inspires me and all the other young players to play freely. “He plays as if the pitch were his own. It’s a great challenge,” noted the Reds’ forward. England call-up pit Ngumoha against Yamal Rio Ngumoha could come up against Yamal later this month. (Photo by Ahmad Mora/Getty Images) Ngumoha’s admiration for Yamal could soon become a personal challenge. This is because England are scheduled to face Croatia on November 12 before travelling to Spain on November 15 at the Metropolitano, with the latter fixture potentially bringing the two young wingers onto the same pitch. At 18, Ngumoha is the youngest player in Tuchel’s November England squad and has already made his senior international debut. Yamal, on the other hand, is an established member of Barcelona and Spain’s setup, and a meeting with the Spaniard would offer Ngumoha an opportunity to test himself against a player whose development he clearly admires.

item.title: Filip Forsberg scores twice as Predators blank Kings
item.description: Los Angeles Kings right wing Alex Laferriere (14) fights for the puck during their game against the Nashville Predators at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Kings entered Tuesday night seeking a bounce-back victory following Saturday’s loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins and looking to establish consistency on home ice. Instead, the club's offensive droughts resurfaced as Los Angeles was shut out for the first time this season, falling 3-0 to the Nashville Predators at Crypto.com Arena. The frustration surrounding another quiet night from the offense was evident after the game. "I think everybody’s probably frustrated," head coach Peter Laviolette said. "We’re here to win hockey games and we’re not getting that done." In a unique matchup featuring a battle of matching surnames — Nashville forward Filip Forsberg facing off against Los Angeles goaltender Anton Forsberg — the Predators' star winger got the upper hand over his counterpart, striking twice to pave the way for a Nashville road win. Coming into the contest, both clubs averaged exactly 3.00 goals per game, reflecting similar scoring metrics on paper. On Tuesday night, however, Nashville simply executed when opportunities arose while the Kings failed to convert on their own looks. "There were point blank chances and rebound chances and just not able to capitalize," Laviolette said. "I don’t think we made the plays quick enough." The Predators broke the ice midway through the opening frame off an unforced error. Nils Hoglander intercepted a pass from Kings defenseman Brian Dumoulin and led a two-on-one odd-man rush down the ice, feeding Filip Forsberg, who buried a one-timer to put Nashville ahead with 14:40 remaining in the first period. The Nashville Predators players celebrate a goal during their game against the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. Dakota Gray - The Sporting Tribune The Nashville Predators players celebrate a goal during their game against the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. After Los Angeles closed the first period strong and carried momentum into the middle frame, the Hoglander-to-Forsberg connection struck again. Halfway through the second period, Hoglander centered a pass to the two-time All-Star at the faceoff dot, where the 32-year-old Swede snapped a shot top-shelf for his seventh goal of the season, doubling the Predators' cushion. An empty-net tally by Adam Wilsby with under two minutes remaining slammed the door on a disappointing night for Los Angeles, dropping the club to 5-9-2 on the year and leaving the locker room searching for answers. item.content:encoded: Los Angeles Kings right wing Alex Laferriere (14) fights for the puck during their game against the Nashville Predators at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. LOS ANGELES — The Los Angeles Kings entered Tuesday night seeking a bounce-back victory following Saturday’s loss to the Pittsburgh Penguins and looking to establish consistency on home ice. Instead, the club's offensive droughts resurfaced as Los Angeles was shut out for the first time this season, falling 3-0 to the Nashville Predators at Crypto.com Arena. "We’re here to win hockey games and we’re not getting that done." Coming into the contest, both clubs averaged exactly 3.00 goals per game, reflecting similar scoring metrics on paper. On Tuesday night, however, Nashville simply executed when opportunities arose while the Kings failed to convert on their own looks. "There were point blank chances and rebound chances and just not able to capitalize," Laviolette said. "I don’t think we made the plays quick enough." The Predators broke the ice midway through the opening frame off an unforced error. Nils Hoglander intercepted a pass from Kings defenseman Brian Dumoulin and led a two-on-one odd-man rush down the ice, feeding Filip Forsberg, who buried a one-timer to put Nashville ahead with 14:40 remaining in the first period. The Nashville Predators players celebrate a goal during their game against the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. Dakota Gray - The Sporting Tribune The Nashville Predators players celebrate a goal during their game against the Los Angeles Kings at Crypto.com Arena on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, in Los Angeles. After Los Angeles closed the first period strong and carried momentum into the middle frame, the Hoglander-to-Forsberg connection struck again. Halfway through the second period, Hoglander centered a pass to the two-time All-Star at the faceoff dot, where the 32-year-old Swede snapped a shot top-shelf for his seventh goal of the season, doubling the Predators' cushion. An empty-net tally by Adam Wilsby with under two minutes remaining slammed the door on a disappointing night for Los Angeles, dropping the club to 5-9-2 on the year and leaving the locker room searching for answers. "I think [we] didn't feel connected out there at all," winger Adrian Kempe said. "Overall, pretty disappointed." While Anton Forsberg kept the Kings within striking distance, Predators goalie Juuse Saros delivered a flawless performance at the opposite end, stopping all 30 shots he faced to record his first shutout of the season. When the offense sputters, wins are hard to come by for Los Angeles. Plain and simple. In Laviolette's first season behind the bench, the Kings are 0-8-1 when scoring two goals or fewer, spotlighting a concerning trend early in the campaign. Los Angeles has struggled to extract wins from tightly contested, low-scoring games — finding success only when the offense is humming. Despite surrendering two goals to his namesake counterpart, Anton Forsberg stood tall as one of the brightest spots on the ice for Los Angeles, turning aside 27 of 29 shots. Yet when the veteran goalie gets the nod, run support remains elusive. In his six starts this season, the Kings are 0-5-1 while averaging a subpar 1.5 goals per game. "He’s played good for us," center Scott Laughton said of Forsberg’s effort. "We need to find a way to find sustained zone time in the offensive zone, wear teams down, where they’re tired and we three-quarter ice them. It’s just not happening right now." In order to climb out of their losing ways, individual accountability across the lineup will be essential moving forward. "I haven’t been good enough," Laughton said. "I need to bring more to this group and I’m sure a lot of guys would say the same." Despite the early-season adversity, the sentiment inside the locker room remains focused on constantly improving and keeping the energy high. "We're a good hockey team," Laughton said. "I believe that. We've got to have that belief in the group and we’ve got to continue to push forward here."

item.title: Carlos Espi talks Mbappe, Ballon d’Or, Mourinho and Premier League interest
item.description: Carlos Espi talks Mbappe, Ballon d’Or, Mourinho and Premier League interest There is no doubt that Kylian Mbappe is one of the best players on the planet, and his second-placed finish on the Ballon d’Or standings reflects the same. His numbers at Real Madrid are staggering, and he has already made the number nine position his own with Los Blancos . The club did, however, see the need to keep a backup player in the position and went on to bring in Carlos Espi – a player who provides a more direct goalscoring threat as a traditional number nine. So far, the duo have worked very well in tandem. While it is Mbappe who starts and hogs a massive part of the minutes, Espi has stepped up with clutch goals when Real Madrid have needed them most. Espi heaps praise on Mbappe Espi and Mbappe in action. (Photo by Francisco Macia/Getty Images) Speaking to the media on duty with the Spain U21 team, the youngster commented on Kylian Mbappe and revealed his two cents on the Frenchman’s quality. “Kylian Mbappe is the best player in the world. To me, he deserved the Ballon d’Or,” he added. He then revealed how just training with the forward taught him a lot and helped him improve. “Every training session I spend with him, I try to learn as much as I can from him, and listen to everything he tells me. “His speed, his dribbling, his goalscoring, it’s incredible to watch, really,” he added. On Jose Mourinho The manager then commented on Jose Mourinho and how the manager was transforming the dressing room into a winning machine. “José Mourinho is incredible,” he began. “He’s very close to us, very demanding, and that’s a very good thing,” he added. Espi appreciated Mourinho’s management. (Photo by Clive Brunskill/Getty Images) Espi then revealed how it felt personally to work with the legendary manager, and how his relationship with the coach was. “It’s great to have him so close to me, telling me what I did well and what I did badly, I’m very happy with José.” Espi speaks on his time at Real Madrid Finally, the player expressed what a privilege it was to play for Real Madrid. “To me, every minute I spend on the pitch for Real Madrid is golden.” “Every opportunity to play is a golden opportunity,” he added. He acknowledged that he was not receiving as many minutes as he liked, but also stressed that he is willing to wait for his chances. “Of course I’d like to play more, every player does, but I just focus on taking full advantage of every opportunity the coach gives me to play.” Finally, Espi revealed how he could have signed for multiple Premier League sides in the summer and how Real Madrid’s arrival on the scene changed everything. “It’s true that I could’ve gone to the Premier League last summer, but when Real Madrid called, I could not say no.” Source: Cadena SER

item.title: Jets Take Parting Shot at Connor Hellebuyck After Beating Devils
item.description: Connor Hellebuyck Jets Devils Getty The Winnipeg Jets organization took a parting shot at former goalie Connor Hellebuyck after beating the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday night. In one of the most highly anticipated games of the year, the Jets beat the Devils 4-2 on Tuesday night in Winnipeg, in Hellebuyck’s return to the city where he spent the first 11 seasons of his NHL career. Dawson Mercer, who was part of the trade package for Hellebuyck, scored twice against his former team as the Jets won their fourth straight game. Meanwhile, the Devils lost with Jake Allen in net, as the team said that starting Hellebuyck would have given the team a lower chance to win the game, something the Jets organization had a field day with after beating New Jersey. Jets Take Parting Shot at Devils On their social media, the Jets made it clear where they stood with the Devils’ decision not to start Hellebuyck against them due to analytical reasons. “Expected Win Probability 100%,” the Jets wrote on their X . Expected Win Probability 100% ✈️ @Wawanesa | #GoJetsGo pic.twitter.com/1SIWKkjSUK — Winnipeg Jets (@NHLJets) November 11, 2026 It’s a brutal message from the Jets to the Devils and their former franchise goalie, Hellebuyck, but it’s one that is deserved, as Hellebuyck gave up on his former team and demanded a trade out of Winnipeg, even deciding not to show up to training camp while awaiting a trade. Devils Look Foolish for Connor Hellebuyck Decision Ever since the Jets announced on their social media that they would be sitting Hellebuyck for this game against the Jets due to analytics, they have been the butt-end of jokes from those in the hockey world, and for good reason, as their reasoning to sit their starting goalie made zero sense. The fact that the Devils pointed to analytics as the reason they didn’t want to start Hellebuyck was laughable and made them look foolish to the entire NHL. It makes you wonder who allowed the Devils’ PR team to release such an outlandish statement, knowing what the reaction to it would be. In the end, though, the Jets got the last laugh, and the Devils look like fools for keeping Hellebuyck out of this game. Meanwhile, the Devils lost with Jake Allen in net, as the team said that starting Hellebuyck would have given the team a lower chance to win the game, something the Jets organization had a field day with after beating New Jersey. Jets Take Parting Shot at Devils On their social media, the Jets made it clear where they stood with the Devils’ decision not to start Hellebuyck against them due to analytical reasons. “Expected Win Probability 100%,” the Jets wrote on their X . Expected Win Probability 100% ✈️ @Wawanesa | #GoJetsGo pic.twitter.com/1SIWKkjSUK — Winnipeg Jets (@NHLJets) November 11, 2026 It’s a brutal message from the Jets to the Devils and their former franchise goalie, Hellebuyck, but it’s one that is deserved, as Hellebuyck gave up on his former team and demanded a trade out of Winnipeg, even deciding not to show up to training camp while awaiting a trade. Devils Look Foolish for Connor Hellebuyck Decision Ever since the Jets announced on their social media that they would be sitting Hellebuyck for this game against the Jets due to analytics, they have been the butt-end of jokes from those in the hockey world, and for good reason, as their reasoning to sit their starting goalie made zero sense. The fact that the Devils pointed to analytics as the reason they didn’t want to start Hellebuyck was laughable and made them look foolish to the entire NHL. It makes you wonder who allowed the Devils’ PR team to release such an outlandish statement, knowing what the reaction to it would be. In the end, though, the Jets got the last laugh, and the Devils look like fools for keeping Hellebuyck out of this game. item.title: Police arrest Abuja man over alleged rape, cyberbullying of women
item.description: The Federal Capital Territory (FCT) Police Command has arrested a man, identified as Usman Mohammed, over alleged rape, sexual assault, cyberbullying and intimidation of women under the pretext of recovering debts owed to him. The Police Public Relations Officer, SP Josephine Adeh, disclosed this in a statement, saying the suspect allegedly targeted women, including widows and other vulnerable persons, through predatory money-lending practices. Adeh said the suspect was arrested on Friday, November 6, 2026, following a report received at the Lugbe Police Station at about 7:05 p.m., alleging that he had been intimidating, sexually assaulting and physically assaulting several women over debts owed to him. She said operatives from the Lugbe Division, led by the Divisional Police Officer, immediately launched efforts to track down the suspect. According to her, the suspect was traced to the Federal Housing Authority (FHA), Lugbe, where police operatives moved to arrest him. However, he allegedly attempted to escape upon sighting the officers by speeding off in his vehicle. The police said the operatives gave chase and eventually intercepted him before he could gain access to the expressway. Adeh said preliminary investigations identified Mohammed as a resident of FHA Lugbe, who allegedly used debt recovery as a pretext to intimidate and exploit his victims. She alleged that, in his latest incident, the suspect lured a woman into his vehicle and drove her to a secluded location in Lugbe, where he sexually assaulted and raped her. The suspect allegedly forced the victim to strip naked and recorded videos of her private parts, which he subsequently used to threaten to expose her publicly and kill her if she failed to meet his repayment demands. The police spokesperson said Mohammed was currently in custody and undergoing further interrogation. She added that he would be charged to court upon the conclusion of investigations. The Commissioner of Police, FCT Command, CP Ahmed Muhammed Sanusi, condemned all forms of violence, sexual exploitation, intimidation and cyberbullying. He urged residents, particularly vulnerable persons, not to suffer in silence but to report cases of abuse, threats, blackmail and other criminal activities to the nearest police station. The Command also provided emergency contact numbers for members of the public: 08032003913 and 08061581938. The post Police arrest Abuja man over alleged rape, cyberbullying of women appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: ‘Took This Personal,’ ‘True Revenge Game’ — NBA World Raves As Paul George Outshines Jaylen Brown in Celtics-76ers Clash With ‘Vintage’ 36-Point Night
item.description: 'Took This Personal,' 'True Revenge Game' — NBA World Raves As Paul George Outshines Jaylen Brown in Celtics-76ers Clash With 'Vintage' 36-Point Night Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown’s first regular-season meeting as opponents headlined Tuesday’s marquee matchup between the Boston Celtics and Philadelphia 76ers. However, Paul George stole the show, leading all scorers with 36 points in Boston’s resounding 123-101 road win. Acquired in the surprising offseason trade that sent Brown to the 76ers, the nine-time All-Star shined in his first game back in Philadelphia. George’s vintage performance drew high praise from around the NBA world, with some contrasting it with his underwhelming, injury-plagued stint with the 76ers, which the 36-year-old addressed after the game. Paul George’s Dominant Return to Philadelphia Fuels Redemption-Season Buzz George shot 14-for-22 overall (63.6%), including 6-for-11 from 3-point range (54.5%), adding 5 rebounds and 1 assist in only 30 minutes. Boston broke a 79-79 tie with a late third-quarter run, and the veteran forward took over from there. He scored 14 consecutive Celtics points in a stretch of just under 4 minutes in the final frame, extending Boston’s lead from 97-82 to 111-87. In contrast, Brown struggled to find his rhythm. The 2024 NBA Finals MVP picked up 2 fouls in the first quarter and his 4th early in the third, finishing with a quiet 13 points on 4-for-9 shooting (44.4%) while logging a game-worst minus-27 plus-minus. Tatum added 21 points for Boston, while Tyrese Maxey led the 76ers with 24. I still got a lot left in the tank.” “The true revenge game today. JB didn’t show up,” one fan reacted. My job is to come in and support JT and be the best version that I can be for him. That was my only focus,” George said . READ MORE: ‘LeBron (James) Gotta Retire,’ ‘Jaylen Brown Is Punching the Air’ — Hoops Fans Lose It Over Jayson Tatum’s ‘Disrespectful’ Poster Dunk on 76ers Star On NBC’s postgame show, George, who battled multiple injuries with the 76ers, spoke to the contrast between his two stops: “I’m a little bit better with more usage, and that’s no knock to my opportunities here with Philly,” George shared. “Quite frankly, I wasn’t healthy to take on the workload that I feel I’m at my best at. item.title: Blázquez double from Rioja assists seals Valencia’s 6-0 Copa del Rey win over Tavernes
item.description: Blázquez double from Rioja assists seals Valencia’s 6-0 Copa del Rey win over Tavernes Aimar Blázquez scored twice from Rioja assists as Valencia beat Tavernes 6-0 at Mestalla, where the hosts were officially the away side. The win follows a 0-3 defeat to Real Madrid and takes Valencia into the second round. Valencia cruised past Tavernes in the Copa del Rey on Tuesday 10 November 2026. The tie was played at the Estadio de Mestalla, yet Valencia were officially the away side in their own stadium. The RFEF had granted Tavernes’ request to stage the match there. Valencia were four goals up inside 23 minutes Raba opened the scoring in the first minute, with Blázquez providing the assist. Raba then turned provider for Duro in the 11th minute. Rioja added the third in the 19th minute after a pass from Martinez. A fourth goal arrived through Elliott in the 23rd minute. Tavernes goalkeeper Mainar kept the margin there three minutes into the second half. He saved a header from Blázquez, who had been set up by Raba. The number 37 struck in the 57th minute and again in the 69th. Danjuma replaced him after 70 minutes, when Gayà also came on for Rioja. Three players were booked. Ugrinic was cautioned in the ninth minute and Montilla of Tavernes in the 22nd. Rioja picked up a yellow card in the 49th minute. Tavernes came closest to a goal when Erik struck the post after a short corner. EFE described the visitors as a sixth-tier club and reported that close to 40 coaches carried their fans to Mestalla. Their municipal ground was not fit for the tie. Mestalla is in its final season before the move to Nou Mestalla. The original 9pm kick-off fell to the RFEF’s postponements A 9pm start had been planned for the tie. Every Copa del Rey match scheduled for that day was called off by the RFEF, and this one was among them. Tavernes reached the first round through the two-legged preliminary round against UD Maracena. The first leg was played at the CD Maracena ground on Sunday 27 September 2026. The two sides drew 1-1 and 0-0. For Valencia, the Real Madrid loss had itself followed a 1-0 win over Elche and a 1-2 defeat to Villarreal. Javier Aguirre said he took positive conclusions from the tie. He welcomed the return of players who had been out long-term. He also said Valencia now need to win in the league. The cup calendar continues with the round of 32 on 16 December. The last 16 follows on 6 January and the quarter-finals on 13 January. The semi-finals are the only two-legged round, with first legs on 10 February and second legs on 3 March. The competition runs until 24 April 2027. Valencia return to league action away to Rayo Vallecano at the Estadio de Vallecas on Saturday 21 November. item.title: Australia used sandpaper even before 2018? Former Aussie spinner Stuart Macgill reveals how he used to rough up balls during matches
item.description: Australia used sandpaper even before 2018? Former Aussie spinner Stuart Macgill reveals how he used to rough up balls during matches originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Former Aussie spinner Stuart MacGill has opened up about some surprising tricks from his playing days. Sandpaper on his thumb helped him change the condition of the ball. His comments raise fresh questions about how new the 2018 Cape Town scandal really was. MORE: Khawaja autobiography highlights: All major talking points from 'Sabr' 'Scratched the daylights out of it!': Stuart MacGill drops shocking sandpaper confession Was sandpaper part of Australian cricket long before the 2018 Cape Town scandal shocked the sporting world? Former Test spinner Stuart MacGill has now offered his own account of life on the field in an earlier era, and it makes for rather uncomfortable reading for those who believed the issue began and ended with one infamous afternoon. MacGill played 44 Tests for Australia between 1998 and 2008, picking up 208 wickets at an average of 29.02. He was widely regarded as one of the most prolific strike bowlers of his generation, and his career ran alongside that of the great Shane Warne. The incidents he described belong to the late 1990s and 2000s, which is well before the March 2018 episode in Cape Town that led to 12-month bans for Steve Smith and David Warner and a nine-month ban for Cameron Bancroft. MORE: Steyn spots irony in Khawaja's Sandpapergate revelation as Broad joins in mocking AUS Stuart MacGill sandpaper admission: How he scratched the ball on his thumb The host got straight to the point and asked whether MacGill had ever used sandpaper. The former leg-spinner did not hesitate, and he went on to explain a clever routine that relied on a small habit of the umpires. During breaks, the match ball would be placed roughly 20 metres beyond the boundary rope, and a fielder would run out to collect it before play resumed. MORE: Usman Khawaja reveals why he waited until retirement to expose Sandpapergate MacGill saw an opportunity in that short run. He fixed a small square of sandpaper to his thumb, picked up the ball after the tea interval, roughed it up and then ripped the paper off before dropping it into the gutter. By the time the first delivery of the session was bowled, no trace of the paper remained. “I’ve used it. What they would do is the umpires, as you’re walking out on the ground, they used to put the ball, sort of about 20 metres over the boundary and leave it there, and you’d run out onto the field, pick it up and go on the field," MacGill said on the Fanatics ​​​​​​podcast. “I taped a little square of sandpaper on my thumb, picked the ball up just after tea, scratched the living daylights out of it, pulled the sandpaper off, chucked it in the gutter before a ball had even been bowled. item.content:encoded: Australia used sandpaper even before 2018? Former Aussie spinner Stuart Macgill reveals how he used to rough up balls during matches originally appeared on Cricket News . Add Cricket News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . KEY TAKEAWAYS: Former Aussie spinner Stuart MacGill has opened up about some surprising tricks from his playing days. Sandpaper on his thumb helped him change the condition of the ball. His comments raise fresh questions about how new the 2018 Cape Town scandal really was. MORE: Khawaja autobiography highlights: All major talking points from 'Sabr' 'Scratched the daylights out of it!': Stuart MacGill drops shocking sandpaper confession Was sandpaper part of Australian cricket long before the 2018 Cape Town scandal shocked the sporting world? Former Test spinner Stuart MacGill has now offered his own account of life on the field in an earlier era, and it makes for rather uncomfortable reading for those who believed the issue began and ended with one infamous afternoon. MacGill played 44 Tests for Australia between 1998 and 2008, picking up 208 wickets at an average of 29.02. He was widely regarded as one of the most prolific strike bowlers of his generation, and his career ran alongside that of the great Shane Warne. The incidents he described belong to the late 1990s and 2000s, which is well before the March 2018 episode in Cape Town that led to 12-month bans for Steve Smith and David Warner and a nine-month ban for Cameron Bancroft. MORE: Steyn spots irony in Khawaja's Sandpapergate revelation as Broad joins in mocking AUS Stuart MacGill sandpaper admission: How he scratched the ball on his thumb The host got straight to the point and asked whether MacGill had ever used sandpaper. The former leg-spinner did not hesitate, and he went on to explain a clever routine that relied on a small habit of the umpires. During breaks, the match ball would be placed roughly 20 metres beyond the boundary rope, and a fielder would run out to collect it before play resumed. MORE: Usman Khawaja reveals why he waited until retirement to expose Sandpapergate MacGill saw an opportunity in that short run. He fixed a small square of sandpaper to his thumb, picked up the ball after the tea interval, roughed it up and then ripped the paper off before dropping it into the gutter. By the time the first delivery of the session was bowled, no trace of the paper remained. “I’ve used it. What they would do is the umpires, as you’re walking out on the ground, they used to put the ball, sort of about 20 metres over the boundary and leave it there, and you’d run out onto the field, pick it up and go on the field," MacGill said on the Fanatics ​​​​​​podcast. “I taped a little square of sandpaper on my thumb, picked the ball up just after tea, scratched the living daylights out of it, pulled the sandpaper off, chucked it in the gutter before a ball had even been bowled. So nobody even knew that I’d done it, apart from all the scratches on the ball!” Not every experiment went to plan, however. MacGill admitted that he tried a few other ideas as well, including one that ended in a rather funny failure. “I also tried a couple of other things. I sewed a piece of sandpaper inside my trousers one time, but unfortunately that got a hole in my strides, so...” he said. MORE: 'Haven’t paid much attention': Starc denies Khawaja's allegation The SCG Swans race trick: How a full toss helped roughen the ball for reverse swing The third story took place at the Sydney Cricket Ground, where MacGill usually bowled from the Paddington End. He explained that a waist-high full toss was a deliberate tactic because it invited the batter to hook or pull the ball in the direction of the Swans race, the tunnel gate at the ground. Whenever the ball ended up there, the fielder who went to collect it would drag it along the wall on his way back, and that scraping could rough up one side of it to help reverse swing. The mark left behind was clearly visible to anyone who looked closely. “I used to bowl from the Paddington end. If I bowled a waist-high full toss, it was an opportunity for the batsman just to swing me straight down the Swans race. On the occasion that the ball did actually go down there, the fieldsman would walk back up scraping the ball against the wall. There was a big red stripe on the wall!” he said. At one point the host teased MacGill with a quip about a fielder wandering around at deep backward square, and the answer opened up the bigger debate. MacGill brought up Darren Lehmann, the former teammate who later became Australia’s coach, and said he believes that the practice has been around since the earliest days of Test cricket. “You know, Boof (Lehmann) reckons it’s been happening since day one in Test cricket, and I think it probably has been. Because we know that everybody’s doing it, it doesn’t feel so bad. Like if I’m playing against South Africa, I know that they’ve done everything that I’ve done, so I don’t feel bad about it,” he said. In 2018, Cricket Australia presented the sandpaper incident as an unprecedented act devised by Warner and Bancroft, but MacGill’s story points to the use of sandpaper by an Australian player almost two decades earlier, at least in his own case. It also lines up with recent remarks from Usman Khawaja, who claimed in his autobiography Sabr that manipulating the ball was routine in the Sheffield Shield and that “it was all of us” in 2018. Stuart Broad's father, Chris Broad and David Warner have also recently been critical of Lehmann’s public stance of innocence, which makes the new comments even more relevant. MORE: 'Couldn't agree more': David Warner and Stuart Broad's father call out Darren Lehmann's hypocrisy as Sandpapergate fallout continues MacGill’s confession shows why the ball-tampering debate is far from over MacGill’s story is entertaining on the surface, but it should also make cricket think hard about its own history. A thumb covered in sandpaper, a patch stitched into trousers and a scraped ball in the SCG tunnel are not accidental acts. They were planned ideas, and the former spinner describes them with the ease of someone who thought it was part of the job. The most worrying part is the “everybody’s doing it” argument. It may feel natural inside a dressing room, but it is exactly the kind of thinking that allows small rule-bending to grow into something bigger. If players believe that rivals are doing the same, the line between a tactic and cheating becomes blurry, and that is how a scandal like Cape Town can happen. That said, MacGill deserves some credit for speaking so openly, as most players from his era have stayed quiet. His honesty gives the sport a chance to talk about what really took place, rather than pretend the problem started in 2018 and ended with three bans. The game’s authorities should treat these comments as a prompt for a broader conversation. Clearer rules, stricter monitoring of the ball and a culture that does not excuse shortcuts would do more good than harsh punishments after every new revelation. Honest talk about the past is the only way to protect the future.
