item.title: Yankees predicted to replace Jazz Chisholm with $24M Gold Glove finalist, Silver Slugger finalist
item.description: Yankees predicted to replace Jazz Chisholm with $24M Gold Glove finalist, Silver Slugger finalist originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The New York Yankees have some major decisions to make this offseason, including potentially parting ways with players who have been with the organization for several seasons. New York has endured back-to-back disappointing playoff performances after reaching the World Series, and changes could be coming to the roster. The Yankees also dealt with several injuries in 2026. Second base and third base are two positions the organization may need to address this winter. “This is where Cashman needs to get creative and swing a surprise blockbuster deal for a third baseman, much like he did with Donaldson (even if that failed to work out). Right now, the Yankees' best options at third are Jose Caballero, who didn't see good results there in 2026, and Anthony Volpe, who is still learning the position and doesn't have the ideal arm strength to handle it," SI's Joe Najarian wrote. Jazz Chisholm Jr. has primarily handled second base over the last couple of seasons, but his future in New York is becoming increasingly uncertain. “As the Yankees look to retool their roster for the 2027 season, there's a massive hole they will need to fill. Second base, manned by Jazz Chisholm Jr. for the last two seasons, will explore free agency and it's likely he will not return to the Bronx," SNY's Phillip Martinez wrote. With Chisholm potentially leaving in free agency, MLB Trade Rumors' Steve Adams believes the Yankees could target Brandon Lowe as a replacement. “There’s never been much doubt about Lowe’s power. He belted 35 homers in 2026 — the second-most of his career and his second straight 30-homer campaign (third in his career). Lowe hit .260/.331/.493 with strong batted-ball metrics (91 mph average exit velocity, 45.6% hard-hit rate, 12.5% barrel rate). By measure of wRC+, Lowe has never been a below-average hitter in any season of his nine-year career, and this season’s 121 mark (21% better than average) was right in line with his career mark of 123,” Adams wrote. This is the type of move many Yankees fans would like to see, especially after the team struggled to get consistent offensive production from its infield last season. With the right additions, New York's lineup could look significantly different in 2027. Lowe played under a $24 million contract with the Pittsburgh Pirates in 2026. The Yankees will need to be aggressive if they want to get back to the top of the American League, and pursuing a proven power hitter like Lowe would be one way to do it. Pakistan vs. Sri Lanka 1st Test, Day 3 Live Score & Updates Welcome to CricketNews.com's live coverage of the 1st Test between Pakistan and Sri Lanka at the Rawalpindi Cricket Stadium in Rawalpindi. Day 3 Lunch: Sri Lanka 221/4 After being reduced to 65/3 early, Sri Lanka mounted a commanding middle-order fightback to reach 221/4 in 60 overs at the Lunch interval. Captain Kusal Mendis dropped anchor alongside De Silva, batting through the morning session to remain unbeaten on 21 off 52 balls in an ongoing 66-run fifth-wicket partnership. Mohammad Abbas (17-8-33-2) and Saqib Khan (20-1-82-2) delivered all four breakthroughs, while Razaullah and Arafat Minhas went wicketless heading into the break. Day 2 Stumps: Sri Lanka 114/3; 1st innings - Pakistan 434/9d Pakistan strengthened their dominance in the first Test, holding a 320-run lead after ending Day 2 with Sri Lanka at 114/3 in their first innings. Sri Lanka suffered an early collapse, losing Pasindu Sooriyabandara (0) and Dinesh Chandimal (1) inside the first four overs. Lahiru Udara offered resistance with 42 off 52 balls, including seven boundaries, before falling to Saqib Khan in the 17th over. Saqib picked up two wickets, while Mohammad Abbas dismissed Sooriyabandara to leave Sri Lanka struggling at 65/3. Kamindu Mendis and Dhananjaya de Silva steadied the innings with an unbeaten 49-run fourth-wicket partnership. Sri Lanka will resume Day 3 at 114/3, trailing Pakistan by 320 runs with seven wickets remaining. Day 2 Tea: Sri Lanka 42/2; 1st innings - Pakistan 434/9d Pakistan continued to dominate the contest after declaring their first innings at 434/9, with Sri Lanka struggling at 42/2 in 12 overs at tea. Mohammad Abbas and debutant Saqib Khan struck early to leave Sri Lanka two wickets down inside the first four overs. Abbas dismissed Pasindu Sooriyabandara for a duck while Saqib removed Dinesh Chandimal for one with an excellent delivery that produced a leading edge. Lahiru Udara offered some resistance with an unbeaten 29 off 35 balls, including four boundaries, while Kamindu Mendis was unbeaten on eight. Sri Lanka will resume the evening session trailing Pakistan by 392 runs, with eight wickets remaining. Day 2 Lunch: Pakistan 390/6 Good start for Pakistan bowlers as Sri Lanka lose two early wickets. Shakeel missed out on his century by a whisker as he departed for 93 runs. After losing nine wickets, Pakistan finally declared their innings closed at 434. A massive total on board, and it is now up to the bowlers to restrict Sri Lanka to a moderate total. Pakistan have lost just one wicket in the first session on Day 2 as they inch closer towards the 400-run mark. A big total loading for the hosts. Saud Shakeel is batting brilliantly, and he is in his 90s. Match resumes at Rawalpindi. The hosts will hope to build on their quality start and hope to add as many runs as possible. Pakistan vs. Sri Lanka 1st Test, Day 1 Score & Updates DAY 1 STUMPS: Pakistan 277/5 (Shakeel 57*, Ghori 3*) Pakistan ended Day 1 at 277/5 after 67.2 overs. Sri Lanka fought back in the final session, picking up two wickets and conceding 65 runs. Debutant Mohammad Taha scored a fighting 51 off 105 balls before falling to Sonal Dinusha. Saud Shakeel remained unbeaten on 57 off 112 deliveries, finally converting his start into a half-century. Salman Agha contributed 16 before being dismissed by Asitha Fernando. Ghazi Ghori was unbeaten on 3 alongside Saud at stumps. Play was stopped due to bad light, with stumps officially called soon after. Only 67.2 overs were bowled on the opening day, with Sri Lanka also struggling with a poor over rate. AT TEA: Pakistan 214/3 (Taha 41*, Shakeel 24*) Pakistan reached 214/3 at tea on Day 1, adding 75 runs and losing just one wicket in the second session. Babar Azam scored a half-century (50 off 58 balls, including seven fours) before being dismissed by Dilshan Madushanka. Madushanka broke the 70-run partnership between Babar and Mohammad Taha, with Kusal Mendis taking the catch behind the stumps. Debutant Mohammad Taha remained unbeaten on 41 off 96 deliveries. Taha survived a dropped catch at 30, when a powerful shot towards short midwicket was not held by Sooriyabandara. Saud Shakeel was unbeaten on 24 off 67 balls, with the pair adding an unbeaten 57-run partnership. Sri Lanka's pacers bowled with greater discipline and extracted movement from the surface, slowing Pakistan's scoring considerably. AT LUNCH: Pakistan 137/2 (Taha 15*, Babar 31*) Pakistan dominated the opening session and reached 137/2 in 29.6 overs at lunch on Day 1 of the first Test against Sri Lanka. Debutant Tayyab Arif smashed a 46-ball half-century, scoring 57 off 51 deliveries, including nine fours and a six. Azan Awais scored 30 off 50 balls as the opening pair added 86 runs off just 97 deliveries. Sri Lanka fought back with two quick wickets, with Milan Rathnayaka dismissing Awais and Asitha Fernando removing Arif. Babar Azam (31*) and debutant Mohammad Taha (15*) remained unbeaten at lunch, putting together an unbeaten partnership. Sri Lanka's seamers struggled with their lines and lengths despite some early movement from the green-looking surface. Toss result: Sri Lanka won the toss and chose to field first. Pakistan will bat on Day 1. Pre-match: Pakistan come into the two-match Test series after beating Sri Lanka 2-1 in the T20Is and winning the ODI tri-series at home, but their red-ball form has been poor. They lost 3-0 to England in their last Test series and have won only two of their last nine Tests. Babar Azam leads a young Pakistan side without Shan Masood, Noman Ali and Sajid Khan, while Mohammad Rizwan missed out despite a double century in the Quaid-e-Azam Trophy. Sri Lanka, under new captain Kusal Mendis, are expected to play an extra spinner in the top seven alongside a three-man pace attack. Sri Lanka are seventh in the WTC standings with one win in six Tests, while defeat here would end Pakistan's hopes of reaching the final. Pakistan lead the head-to-head 23-17 from 59 Tests, and the pitch in Rawalpindi is expected to be flat, especially in the first two days. (Photo by Altan Gocher / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images) Getty The Cleveland Cavaliers head coach is under mounting pressure to deliver amid the team’s early-season struggles. Cavaliers head coach Kenny Atkinson is facing growing scrutiny and mounting job pressure amid a disappointing 5-6 start to the 2026-2027 NBA season. Kenny Atkinson’s Future With The Cavaliers In Question Getty CLEVELAND, OHIO – NOVEMBER 02: Head coach Kenny Atkinson of the Cleveland Cavaliers reacts during the third quarter against the Oklahoma City Thunder at Rocket Arena on November 02, 2026 in Cleveland, Ohio. The Thunder defeated the Cavaliers 117-112. (Photo by Jason Miller/Getty Images) On SiriusXM NBA Radio, NBA insider Marc Stein highlighted that Atkinson’s future is a situation to watch closely following the team’s sluggish progress and the lingering questions from their rough Eastern Conference Finals exit. “It’s been a long time since the Cavs got to the Conference Finals without LeBron James on their roster,” Stein said. “But the Conference Finals against the Knicks were so bad that the questions started there. The Cavs decided to back Kenny Atkinson then. But yeah, I mean, it has been a very worrisome start to the season, and I think we have to keep a very close eye on this.” "I think we have to keep a very close eye on this" @TheSteinLine talks to @BGeltzNBA about the Cavs early season struggles Hear Deals and Dunks weekdays at 1 PM ET https://t.co/uGOfTUanJR pic.twitter.com/jFEoVRxAv8 — SiriusXM NBA Radio (@SiriusXMNBA) November 10, 2026 Atkinson notably guided the Cavaliers to a franchise-record 64-win season in his debut 2024-2025 year, but championship-or-bust expectations in Cleveland have shortened the leash following recent slow starts and high-profile meltdowns. Cavaliers’ 5-6 start to the 2026-2027 NBA season stems largely from defensive lapses, starting lineup chemistry issues, and early-season injuries. After reaching the Eastern Conference Finals a year ago, Cleveland entered the campaign with high expectations, yet they have dropped four of their last five games, including a 124-112 loss to an injury-depleted Charlotte Hornets squad. A major driver of the slump is the sharp decline of 37-year-old guard James Harden , who is averaging a career-low 36.4% from the field and 15.3 points per game while drawing heavy criticism for a lack of defensive effort. Compounding these on-court issues is a wave of early injuries and inconsistent rotation management. Key contributors such as Jarrett Allen, Peyton Watson, Sam Merrill , and Jaylon Tyson have missed time. NBA Analyst Kevin O’Connor Believes Roster Is A Bigger Problem Than The Cavaliers Coach Getty Head coach Kenny Atkinson of the Cleveland Cavaliers during the NBA and FIBA’s Basketball Without Borders Next Up 2026 event at Basketball Development Centre in Istanbul, Turkey on August 29, 2026. (Photo by Altan Gocher / Hans Lucas / AFP via Getty Images) NBA analyst Kevin O’Connor believes the Cavaliers’ underwhelming start to the season stems primarily from flawed roster construction rather than head coach Kenny Atkinson. For O’Connor, a coaching change will not solve the team’s deeper personnel issues. He specifically pointed out that the backcourt pairing of Donovan Mitchell and James Harden is an awkward fit, largely because Harden “looks old,” is struggling to finish at the rim, and appears close to falling off a cliff. “I don’t think Cleveland is going to keep Kenny Atkinson all year long. I don’t think the coaching is necessarily the problem. It’s a problem, but not the problem,” O’Connor said. “James Harden looks old. It’s just the reality of it now.” “This Cleveland team just feels flawed to me, with the top four. Mitchell and Harden is an imperfect backcourt. Mobley and Allen is an imperfect frontcourt, and then a bench that I don’t really think is that good,” he added. The Cavaliers, nonetheless, still have a long season ahead to turn things around and reach the same heights they did last season. However, they must decide now if a change is necessary or continue on with what they are trying to build this early in the season. item.title: Duke’s Jon Scheyer gives Michigan State its flowers after close loss
item.description: David Banks-Imagn Images Duke’s Jon Scheyer gives Michigan State its flowers after close loss appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Duke struggled against Michigan State’s swarming defense on Tuesday , absorbing a tough loss, 79-73, in the State Farm Champions Classic at United Center in Chicago. The No. 2 Blue Devils suffered their first loss , while the No. 5 Spartans remained undefeated in three games. Duke also bowed to Michigan State for the first time in five meetings in the annual tournament. The Spartans held the Blue Devils to just 33.3% shooting, including 7-of-29 from beyond the arc. Duke gave up 16 points on 13 turnovers. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) In the postgame conference, Blue Devils coach Jon Scheyer tipped his hat to the Spartans, touting their readiness and cohesion. “Congrats to Michigan State. They 100% deserved to win. I thought they outcompeted us. They played more together. (Jeremy) Fears controlled the whole game. I thought the difference was their role players. They were incredible. (Cam) Ward, what he did in the first half changed the game,” said Scheyer in the video posted by Carolina Blitz. Jon Scheyer’s opening statement after Duke’s 79-73 loss to Michigan State. pic.twitter.com/W9c6Fj5VJQ — Carolina Blitz (@KeepBlitzin) November 11, 2026 Fears had 18 points, seven rebounds, and 11 assists, while Ward added 14 points and six rebounds in 20 minutes off the bench. John Blackwell led Duke with 17 points and five rebounds. He went 5-of-16 from the field. Patrick Ngongba II added 11 points, seven rebounds, six assists, and four blocks. Scheyer pointed out Duke’s lack of synergy and vowed to play better. “For me, it was a little out-of-body experience. I thought we were not connected. That’s just the bottom line. We’re gonna fix it. I can promise you that much. Our fans deserved better. That was not a good performance tonight,” added Scheyer. Duke will try to bounce back against SIU Edwardsville on Friday. item.title: CNG to save Kano tricycle riders ₦8,200 daily — MDGIF
item.description: Commercial tricycle operators in Kano State could save about ₦8,200 daily on fuel costs by switching from petrol to Compressed Natural Gas (CNG), the Executive Director of the Midstream and Downstream Gas Infrastructure Fund (MDGIF), Oluwole Adama, has said. Adama disclosed this on Tuesday during the commissioning of two Liquefied Compressed Natural Gas (LCNG) facilities established by the MDGIF in partnership with Rolling Energy Limited in Kano. He explained that an operator who spends about ₦14,200 daily on 10 litres of petrol would spend approximately ₦6,000 on CNG for the equivalent energy, resulting in a daily saving of ₦8,200. According to him, the savings could amount to nearly ₦250,000 monthly, providing tricycle operators with additional income to meet household expenses, pay their children’s school fees and save towards owning their tricycles. “Here in Kano, a litre of petrol sells for about ₦1,420, while the same amount of energy from CNG costs about ₦600. That is less than half the price,” Adama said. The two facilities commissioned are the LCNG Mother Station at Tamburawa and a Daughter Station at Hotoro Quarters in Tarauni Local Government Area. Adama said the facilities could support the refuelling of up to 2,500 cars and tricycles daily, while also supplying gas to other refuelling stations. He added that they could serve up to 200 trucks daily, helping to reduce transportation costs and ease the movement of goods from Kano to other parts of the country. The MDGIF executive director disclosed that the Tamburawa Mother Station had the capacity to handle 300,000 standard cubic metres of gas daily. He urged fleet owners, transport unions, businesses and investors to take advantage of the facilities, while calling on Rolling Energy to maintain high safety standards and ensure reliable services. Earlier, the Founder and Chief Executive Officer of Rolling Energy Limited, Mubarak Umar Danbatta, said the projects would bring gas supply closer to businesses and investors in Northern Nigeria. He explained that the development would reduce the cost and logistical challenges associated with transporting gas over long distances, making it easier for businesses to establish CNG stations and industries that depend on natural gas. Danbatta said his company previously travelled hundreds of kilometres from Abuja to source CNG from Ajaokuta and Obajana in Kogi State before transporting it to supply its stations. “What Rolling Energy and MDGIF are doing here in Kano is changing that model. We are bringing gas closer to the people,” he said. He disclosed that the Tamburawa facility had a designed gas-handling capacity of five million standard cubic feet daily, with two LNG storage tanks of 55 metric tonnes each, while the Hotoro station had a storage capacity of eight metric tonnes. According to him, the projects formed part of a wider partnership with MDGIF to establish 10 gas stations, eight planned gas-to-power facilities and an LNG and CNG transportation network. He said the partnership also had plans to expand its operations to Kaduna, Borno, Jigawa, Katsina, Sokoto and Zamfara states. item.title: From Jersey to Somalia... via Liverpool & Man City
item.description: Somalia midfielder Jarma Mohamed moved to eighth-tier Jersey Bulls in the summer [Lauren Queree/Jersey Bulls] Not many 21-year-olds can say they have played international football, had spells at Liverpool and Manchester City and are now playing in non-league after being spotted on a mobile app. But Jarma Mohamed's footballing journey is not that of your typical midfielder. The combative playmaker has been recalled to Somalia's side for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers with Ghana this month, capping a rollercoaster year for the Liverpudlian. "My mum was probably fed up with me just booting stuff in the house, so she got me involved as early as I could," Mohamed jokes with BBC Sport as he talks about the start of his footballing journey. "When I was three she was begging teams to take me because the age that you're allowed is four. "Eventually someone saw me playing and it turned out to be an Everton scout, so I ended up playing for Everton from four and then at that age between four to nine you can play for a few teams. "It was at Liverpool and Everton, eventually chose Liverpool at nine, then signed for Man City at 11. "I came out of Man City and got a scholarship at Wigan, which is one of the best memories of playing football, having a two-year deal, playing day-in, day-out, full-time schedule, staying in digs up in Wigan, travelling up and down the country for away games, performing, picking up the armband a few times, FA Youth Cup, things like that." Jersey Bulls' midfielder Mohamed wins historic call-up Jersey Bulls sign Somalia midfielder Mohamed Mohamed featured alongside players including Jayden Danns at Liverpool and England stars Rico Lewis and Nico O'Reilly at Manchester City. He was released by Wigan in 2024 and spent time in non-league football with Bamber Bridge and Newcastle Town. "I could go abroad and do something, but I wasn't really too sure and I'd been playing showcase games with a company called Player, who basically put players in front of teams, they have an app, which is like a LinkedIn for footballers. "Jersey Bulls were on the app looking for players and, long story short, the owner of Player put me in contact with Jersey Bulls. item.content:encoded: Somalia midfielder Jarma Mohamed moved to eighth-tier Jersey Bulls in the summer [Lauren Queree/Jersey Bulls] Not many 21-year-olds can say they have played international football, had spells at Liverpool and Manchester City and are now playing in non-league after being spotted on a mobile app. But Jarma Mohamed's footballing journey is not that of your typical midfielder. The combative playmaker has been recalled to Somalia's side for their Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers with Ghana this month, capping a rollercoaster year for the Liverpudlian. "My mum was probably fed up with me just booting stuff in the house, so she got me involved as early as I could," Mohamed jokes with BBC Sport as he talks about the start of his footballing journey. "When I was three she was begging teams to take me because the age that you're allowed is four. "Eventually someone saw me playing and it turned out to be an Everton scout, so I ended up playing for Everton from four and then at that age between four to nine you can play for a few teams. "It was at Liverpool and Everton, eventually chose Liverpool at nine, then signed for Man City at 11. "I came out of Man City and got a scholarship at Wigan, which is one of the best memories of playing football, having a two-year deal, playing day-in, day-out, full-time schedule, staying in digs up in Wigan, travelling up and down the country for away games, performing, picking up the armband a few times, FA Youth Cup, things like that." Jersey Bulls' midfielder Mohamed wins historic call-up Jersey Bulls sign Somalia midfielder Mohamed Mohamed featured alongside players including Jayden Danns at Liverpool and England stars Rico Lewis and Nico O'Reilly at Manchester City. He was released by Wigan in 2024 and spent time in non-league football with Bamber Bridge and Newcastle Town. His career came to a crossroads in the summer, when Isthmian League South central side Jersey Bulls spotted him on an app for footballers. "I was thinking what do I want to do?," he said. "I could go abroad and do something, but I wasn't really too sure and I'd been playing showcase games with a company called Player, who basically put players in front of teams, they have an app, which is like a LinkedIn for footballers. "Jersey Bulls were on the app looking for players and, long story short, the owner of Player put me in contact with Jersey Bulls. "I know the club's amateur and no-one gets paid, but we worked out a job that aligns with the things that I do, obviously me having Uefa C licence coaching is something that I'd easily do and I've come over and done it." 'Everyone's really together' Jarma Mohamed and his Jersey Bulls team-mates have yet to lose a league game this season [BBC] Mohamed now works as a youth coach in the island, while also anchoring the midfield of a Jersey Bulls side riding high in the eighth tier of English football. Born in Toxteth, Mohamed's Somalian grandfather moved to Liverpool, part of a large Somali community in the city. It is that heritage that has allowed him to play for a side ranked 200th in the world - the lowest of any team to progress to Afcon's final round of qualifiers. He made his Somalia debut against Mauritius in March as the Ocean Stars reached the final qualifying stages for Afcon for the first time in their history - they beat the island nation on penalties after two goalless draws. "It was a random Wednesday afternoon in my kitchen and I was made up," Mohamed says of the moment he was asked to first join the Somalia squad earlier this year. "I could physically see the community close to home, and going out to the camp and experiencing what that's like, it really lit a fire that I didn't even know I could get as far as trying to push my football career." He is part of a Somali squad made up of more players from the global diaspora than those born in the country itself. Having reached the qualifying stage for next summer's tournament, the lowest ranked side left face a tough group against three-time champions Ivory Coast, Gambia and Ghana - who have won the tournament four times and drew 0-0 with England in the group stage of this summer's World Cup. "Everyone's from different parts of the world, you have lads who are Dutch, from Finland, Italy, there's another scouse with me in the team," Mohamed said. "When we're all there, and even lads who are local and playing in the Somali league, everyone's just one family. "That's one thing which we're really good at, we're together as a team, there's no egos. "Everyone's just really together and wanting to get results for the country, which I feel is very important." 'You can only play what's in front of you' Somalia were narrowly beaten by the Ivory Coast in September [Getty Images] In their first two qualifying matches Somalia have not let themselves down. Gambia scored an 83rd-minute winner to overcome them in their opening game, while an Ivory Coast side boasting Real Madrid's summer signing Yan Diomande, Atalanta's Franck Kessie and former Arsenal winger Nicolas Pepe scored in the 89th minute and the fifth minute added time to earn a 2-0 win. It means the Somalis are second-from-bottom of their group on goal difference from a Ghana side managed by former Real Madrid boss Carlos Queiroz who have lost their opening two matches. With the tense security situation in Somalia the Ocean Stars have played all their qualifiers away from home and will face Ghana in their back-to-back matches in Accra. So how will Mohamed, who plays in front of sparse crowds in small grounds in the area south of London, approach facing opponents who ply their trade in the biggest leagues in the world? "The same way I treat every game, you can only play what's in front of you," he added. "If you play the name or an occasion you're losing before you've even kicked a ball. "I just play who's in front of me and keep it at that. "You know the players' levels, the qualities that they have that you have to respect, but you also have to back yourself. "You're sharing the same pitch for a reason, it's not by accident." And can the Ocean Stars make next summer's tournament in Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania? "The aim is to qualify," he added. "If you come to do nothing less than that you may as well stay home. "In the two games we've had previously against Ivory Coast and Gambia we've shown that we can compete. "If you come to play for the experience or 'we're just happy to be there', then there's no point in coming. "We need to come to try and win." Related internet links Jersey Bulls

item.title: National Champion QB Drops Bold Theory Behind Indiana’s Sudden Drop in Rankings
item.description: BLOOMINGTON, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 12: Indiana Hoosiers head coach Curt Cignetti looks up during the second half against the Howard Bison at Memorial Stadium on September 12, 2026 in Bloomington, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) Getty The Indiana Hoosiers trended for all the wrong reasons Tuesday night. Fans and analysts started believing IU became punished for taking a bye, dropping five spots in the College Football Playoff rankings. Many chimed in, but Danny Kanell believes there’s a deeper theory. The 1993 national champion quarterback for Florida State dropped his bold take following the ranking reveal. The now CBS Sports analyst has reason to believe Curt Cignetti’s past words may have played a role here. “Indiana drops 5 spots on a BYE week. Looks like that committee didn’t appreciate Curt Cignetti’s comments this week,” Kanell posted on the social media website X, formerly known as Twitter. Looks like it’s time to revisit those Cignetti words. Tracing Back to Curt Cignetti’s CFP Rip Cignetti called out a bias the College Football Playoff committee shows toward the SEC. All during a November press conference before the Hoosiers had their bye. “SEC gets a lot of love from ESPN and all their writers that they don’t technically pay but march to their drum,” Cignetti ranted toward reporters. “And that’s why you see all these SEC teams up there and some good two-loss teams from the Big Ten not quite as high.” Cignetti ended with: “But like I said, it’s all gonna play out on the field.” Indiana did just that last year in breezing through 16-0 overall. That included toppling longtime SEC heavyweight Alabama with a 38-3 rout in the Rose Bowl. IU then took down two more heavyweights from outside the SEC: Oregon in the Peach Bowl (56-22) then Miami for the national championship (27-21). But now Kanell believes that Cignetti rant likely doomed his team when the committee formed the newest rankings. Other Theories Sprout Behind Indiana’s Drop Kanell isn’t the only national college football media personality who reacted to the stunning drop. College football insider for On3/Rivals Brett McMurphy called out another aspect attached to IU. “Indiana doesn’t need to worry about dropping five spots to No. 9. The Hoosiers have their non-conference schedule to boost their resume,” McMurphy posted on X. Richard Johnson of CBS Sports became more relentless toward Indiana. “Indiana, it’s simple! If you don’t like that seed that you’re in right now, go beat a ranked USC team!” Johnson said during a broadcast. "Indiana, it's simple! Speaking of the Trojans, they fell into this stunner: South Carolina jumping them at No. 17. The Gamecocks previously were 23rd but beating Texas A&M clearly helped the other SC. Previous No. 1 Miami significantly dropped too, falling down to seventh after taking the Saturday loss to Notre Dame. But again, the Hoosiers dominated the CFP headlines with their five-spot drop. item.title: Kidnappers: I’ll sign execution warrant even for my father – Okpebholo
item.description: Edo State Governor, Monday Okpebholo, has vowed to sign the death warrants of convicted kidnappers, regardless of their relationship with him, declaring that he would personally supervise their execution. The governor said he would not spare anyone found guilty of kidnapping, even if the convict were his father or a close family member. Okpebholo spoke in a video shared by TheCable on Tuesday, amid efforts by his administration to enforce the state’s law prescribing the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. “I pray our brothers are not involved because I will sign it. Even if it is my father, I will sign it. The truth is this: we just have to get some bad elements out of the system for the system to stand. “Because somebody will die. But these people are the ones killing people. How many people have we killed?” he said. The governor defended the proposed executions by highlighting the trauma and physical injuries suffered by victims of kidnapping. He cited an incident involving a woman who was allegedly pushed during an abduction attempt, saying the fear and trauma she experienced could have resulted in her death. He also referred to an attack on the state’s Chief Judge, who he said sustained serious injuries, including the loss of the use of one hand, during an encounter with kidnappers. “Just look at the way they were pushing that woman down there. Supposing she died at that, because of fear, only fear. It’s enough for her to die. People have gone through trauma. “Even our Chief Judge, if you see our Chief Judge, one of his hands was cut off by kidnappers,” he added. Okpebholo said he had contacted the state Attorney-General to ascertain the status of the relevant documents and was awaiting further action. He, however, vowed to pursue the cases through the appeal process, insisting that convicted kidnappers would not be allowed to escape punishment. “But we still follow them up on the appeal. We won’t just let them go like that. So we will get to wherever they stop, we will take them from there. We will not spare anybody. “I stand, if I see this paper today, now, I will sign it and I will even supervise the killing,” he said. The governor’s comments come amid the implementation of the Edo State Kidnapping Prohibition (Amendment) Law, 2025, which introduced the death penalty for kidnapping offences resulting in the death of victims. The Edo State House of Assembly passed the amendment in February 2025, and Okpebholo signed it into law later that month. Under the amended law, kidnapping offences in which victims survive attract life imprisonment, while those directly involved in abductions resulting in the death of victims face capital punishment. The law also prescribes penalties for individuals who aid, abet or provide support for kidnapping activities. In September 2026, four men were sentenced to death by a special criminal court in Edo State over the abduction of a woman at the Vegetable Market along Airpor

item.title: William Nylander ‘Can Play Better,’ Says Maple Leafs HC Jim Hiller
item.description: William Nylander Jim Hiller Maple Leafs Getty Toronto Maple Leafs head coach Jim Hiller said that star forward William Nylander “can play better” after the team lost yet again. The Maple Leafs lost 6-3 to the Colorado Avalanche on Tuesday night for their fourth straight defeat, dropping the team to 8-10-2 on the season through their first 20 games. Nylander was held off the scoresheet while also being a -4 for the team, by far the worst +/- of any player on the ice for the Maple Leafs. After the game, the team’s head coach said that his star winger needs to be better. William Nylander Struggling for Maple Leafs Speaking to reporters following the Maple Leafs’ 6-3 loss to the Avalanche on Tuesday, Hiller said that he wants Nylander to play better, and he believes that the player feels the same way about his play. “I know he can play better than he is right now. I think that’s a pretty fair statement. If you asked him, I think he’d agree,” Hiller said. Jim Hiller on William Nylander: “I know he can play better than he is right now. I think that’s a pretty fair statement. If you asked him, I think he’d agree.” @sdpnsports — Jesse Blake (@JesseBlake) November 11, 2026 Maple Leafs Need More From Star Winger The Maple Leafs have lost four straight games, and in those four losses, Nylander has scored just 1 goal with 0 assists. Given that he is one of the team’s highest-paid players at $11.5 million, he absolutely needs to produce, or else the team will be in trouble keeping pace, scoring-wise, with other teams. This season, Nylander has 11 goals and 11 assists for 22 points, so overall he’s had a decent season scoring-wise. But with the Maple Leafs really struggling right now during the team’s current losing skid, Nylander’s struggles are really starting to stand out, and that’s why Hiller called on him to pick up his play, as Toronto needs him to light the lamp, especially with fellow star winger Kirill Marchenko currently out of the team’s lineup with an injury. That being said, Nylander is far from the only Maple Leafs player who is struggling to score right now, so these losses are not all on him. But when you have one of the highest cap hits on the team, you need to score, or else the team is going to struggle to win games. This article was originally published on HEAVY The post William Nylander ‘Can Play Better,’ Says Maple Leafs HC Jim Hiller appeared first on HEAVY .

item.title: French far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 presidential race
item.description: Far-right pundit Eric ⁠Zemmour on Tuesday officially announced he will run for the French presidency. A politician with a prominent anti-Islam and anti-immigrant ​stance, he vows to "preserve a French France".

item.title: Celtics star Jayson Tatum opens up on making LeBron James his first poster victim since injury
item.description: Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images Celtics star Jayson Tatum opens up on making LeBron James his first poster victim since injury appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jayson Tatum turned back the clock against the Philadelphia 76ers on Tuesday night, and the Boston Celtics star admitted that his poster dunk on LeBron James meant more to him than just two points . Midway through the third quarter, Tatum split a double team, drove hard to the rim and threw down a one-handed slam right over James . After the game, Tatum explained why the play felt so special. “It just kind of felt good to finish through contact. It’s been about 19 months since I dunked on somebody. Just to kind of get my legs back, feeling good, it’s a basketball play,” the 28-year-old said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Jayson Tatum on dunking on LeBron James : "It just kind of felt good to finish through contact. It's been about 19 months since I dunked on somebody. Just to kind of get my legs back, feeling good, it's a basketball play" pic.twitter.com/wlsIgAtwVY — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) November 11, 2026 That stretch without a poster dunk speaks to the long road Tatum has traveled. The six-time All-Star tore his right Achilles tendon during the second round of the 2025 playoffs, an injury that sidelined him for much of the 2025-26 season . He finally made his return on March 6 against the Dallas Mavericks. Ahead of that return, ESPN’s Shams Charania reported that the mental side of regaining confidence in his leg was the biggest hurdle for Tatum , which makes his comments about getting his legs back all the more meaningful. Now, Tatum looks like he is regaining his explosiveness. The dunk also brought back memories of one of the most iconic moments of his career, when he posterized James as a rookie in Game 7 of the 2018 Eastern Conference Finals . That one came in a losing effort, but this time, Tatum and the Celtics came out on top. Boston cruised to a 123-101 win over Philadelphia. Tatum finished with 21 points on 8-of-17 shooting, along with six rebounds, four assists and two blocks. Paul George led the way with 36 points against his former team , while Payton Pritchard chipped in 18. The win carried extra meaning, as it was Tatum’s first matchup against Jaylen Brown since his longtime teammate was traded to the Sixers. The victory improved Boston to 9-2 on the season. Next up is a road date with the Toronto Raptors on Wednesday. Related: Kevin O’Connor explains why Paul George is ‘better fit’ for Jayson Tatum than Jaylen Brown Related: 76ers’ Joel Embiid calls Paul George Celtics’ ‘best player’

item.title: Padres Sign Right-Handed Starter in First Offseason Move of 2026
item.description: Apr 25, 2024; Denver, Colorado, USA; Detailed view of the cap and glove of pitcher Randy Vásquez (98) (not pictured) in seventh inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-USA TODAY Sports | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Lewis Masella, Site Editor The San Diego Padres have made their first move of the 2026 offseason, signing right-hander Ryan Weiss to a one-year, $1.85 million deal with a $4 million club option for 2028. How might the signing affect San Diego’s offseason plans moving forward? Here is a look at how Weiss might fill out the Padres’ 2027 rotation, and their remaining plans for the 2026 offseason. Mar 14, 2022; Scottsdale, AZ, USA; Arizona Diamondbacks pitcher Ryan Weiss during spring training practice at Salt River Fields. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect A Rollercoaster Professional Career Prior to 2026, Weiss had played for two MLB organizations (Arizona Diamondbacks and Kansas City Royals), several independent leagues, the Chinese Professional Baseball League and the Korean Baseball Organization. He struggled to find a groove in the minor leagues, posting a career 4.99 ERA in 389 2/3 innings of work. Weiss’s 1.453 WHIP and .275 opponent batting average in the minors aren’t inspiring confidence either. Welcome to San Diego, Ryan! We have signed right-handed pitcher Ryan Weiss to a one-year contract with a club option for the 2028 season. https://t.co/NBubyHCUdg — San Diego Padres (@Padres) November 11, 2026 It has been a long and difficult road to get to the majors. The right-hander reinvented himself in Korea, joining the Hanwha Eagles of the KBO. From 2024-25, Weiss posted a 3.16 ERA in 270 1/3 innings pitched. item.content:encoded: Apr 25, 2024; Denver, Colorado, USA; Detailed view of the cap and glove of pitcher Randy Vásquez (98) (not pictured) in seventh inning against the Colorado Rockies at Coors Field. Mandatory Credit: Ron Chenoy-USA TODAY Sports | Source: Lastwordonsports.com - Lewis Masella, Site Editor The San Diego Padres have made their first move of the 2026 offseason, signing right-hander Ryan Weiss to a one-year, $1.85 million deal with a $4 million club option for 2028. How might the signing affect San Diego’s offseason plans moving forward? Here is a look at how Weiss might fill out the Padres’ 2027 rotation, and their remaining plans for the 2026 offseason. Mar 14, 2022; Scottsdale, AZ, USA; Arizona Diamondbacks pitcher Ryan Weiss during spring training practice at Salt River Fields. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect A Rollercoaster Professional Career Prior to 2026, Weiss had played for two MLB organizations (Arizona Diamondbacks and Kansas City Royals), several independent leagues, the Chinese Professional Baseball League and the Korean Baseball Organization. He struggled to find a groove in the minor leagues, posting a career 4.99 ERA in 389 2/3 innings of work. Weiss’s 1.453 WHIP and .275 opponent batting average in the minors aren’t inspiring confidence either. Welcome to San Diego, Ryan! We have signed right-handed pitcher Ryan Weiss to a one-year contract with a club option for the 2028 season. https://t.co/NBubyHCUdg — San Diego Padres (@Padres) November 11, 2026 It has been a long and difficult road to get to the majors. The right-hander reinvented himself in Korea, joining the Hanwha Eagles of the KBO. From 2024-25, Weiss posted a 3.16 ERA in 270 1/3 innings pitched. The righty was especially potent in 2025, with a 2.87 ERA across 178 2/3 innings of work with the Eagles. In 30 starts, Weiss won 16 games with 207 strikeouts. That production earned Weiss a one-year, $2.6 million contract with the Houston Astros. He cracked the Opening Day roster before being sent back to the minors after struggling. Weiss allowed 22 earned runs across 26 innings. That being said, he ended the season well. Weiss finished the minor-league season with a 1.37 ERA in his final 19 2/3 innings. Filling Out Rotation Depth Weiss immediately bolsters a group in sore need of starting pitching depth . Prior to the signing, the Padres’ projected starting rotation is comprised of Joe Musgrove , Randy Vásquez , JP Sears , Jhony Brito and Kyle Hart . Vásquez is the only legitimate starter of the group. Musgrove’s spot in the 2027 rotation is not locked down, Sears has struggled at the big-league level, and Brito and Hart have been serviceable bulk relievers at best. Despite his lack of big-league experience, Weiss’s stuff is solid. He features five pitches in his mix, including a four-seamer, sinker, changeup, sweeper, and curveball. His sweeper and changeup are his best pitches (32.4 and 37.9 whiff percentage), combined with a solid 95.2 mph four-seam fastball (95.3 is RHP average). Weiss is probably the first of many signings by general manager A.J. Preller to fill out San Diego’s rotation depth for 2027. The Last Word The Padres entered this offseason with glaring holes in their roster. None was as bad as the rotation. With ace Michael King , Walker Buehler , Nick Pivetta , Robbie Ray , Griffin Canning , Lucas Giolito, and Casey Mize all key Padres free agents , San Diego desperately needs starting pitching. Weiss doesn’t fully address that problem, but he is the beginning of a solution. With the GM Meetings in Las Vegas currently going on, it won’t be surprising to see a few more moves from Preller before the end of the week. The Padres have been linked to several big-name starting pitchers this offseason, including the likes of ace Tarik Skubal . King and Pivetta are also potential returners, even after San Diego declined Pivetta’s club option . No matter what happens, San Diego will need to keep adding to fill out their rotation. Regardless, signing Weiss is the start of what could be the most productive Padres’ offseason in years. item.title: Jaguars GM shuts down ‘F them picks’ approach ahead of NFL trade deadline
item.description: Credit: Travis Register-Imagn Images Jaguars GM shuts down ‘F them picks’ approach ahead of NFL trade deadline appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Jacksonville Jaguars general manager James Gladstone has already made three significant moves to strengthen the team’s defense ahead of the NFL trade deadline. Though Gladstone has parted with valuable draft capital to improve Jacksonville’s chances of making a deep playoff run, he has made it clear that the team is not following the popular ‘F them picks’ philosophy. While explaining the Jaguars’ mindset and approach to roster building ahead of the trade deadline, Gladstone addressed the perception surrounding the team’s willingness to trade draft selections. “Down the road, I think there’s a layer to what you’re articulating there, that’s a part of it for sure,” Gladstone said. “I know that the idea of F them picks has kind of taken a hold and it’s a headline, but you know it’s really not the approach or the process.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Gladstone then explained that Jacksonville’s strategy involves carefully balancing draft capital, free agency and compensatory selections rather than simply sacrificing picks without considering the long-term consequences. “It’s a very symbiotic process that encompasses a lot of layers to it,” he added. “But it’s certainly not F them picks. While that’s been characterized as the approach, it’s not necessarily that we actually value picks. We don’t always use them on the three days that exist in April.” The Jaguars acquired Philadelphia Eagles defensive tackle Jordan Davis, Atlanta Falcons safety Jessie Bates III, and New Orleans Saints defensive tackle Davon Godchaux in three separate trades on Monday. The moves came as Jacksonville looked to address key defensive needs. Still, the cost of those acquisitions means Jacksonville has committed significant future draft capital to its playoff push. The team will now need its new additions to deliver on the field as it enters the second half of the season. The Jaguars entered the week with a 6-2 record after their win over the Baltimore Ravens and a three-game lead in the AFC South. Related: Colts headline 3 biggest losers of 2026 NFL trade deadline after keeping Jonathan Taylor Related: Adam Schefter reveals how quickly Jaguars’ Jordan Davis trade with Eagles came together

item.title: Josh Downs trade: Chiefs fantasy football impact as Patrick Mahomes gets much-needed WR
item.description: Josh Downs trade: Chiefs fantasy football impact as Patrick Mahomes gets much-needed WR appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Patrick Mahomes just got another weapon . Fantasy football managers should pay attention. The Kansas City Chiefs have acquired Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Downs giving Mahomes a much-needed separator who can work underneath and punish defenses over the middle. With injuries disrupting Kansas City’s receiving corps, Downs could become an important piece of Andy Reid’s offense. The trade also creates intriguing fantasy possibilities for Mahomes, Rashee Rice, Travis Kelce, and the rest of the Chiefs’ skill-position players. This could change how Kansas City’s offense operates during the most important stretch of the fantasy football season. Impressive season Denny Medley-Imagn Images Kansas City’s 2026 campaign has been pretty impressive under offensive coordinator Eric Bieniemy. The Chiefs opened with four consecutive victories behind Mahomes’ steady play and Kenneth Walker III’s explosive rushing production. However, consecutive road defeats against Seattle and Denver exposed a glaring lack of separation on the perimeter. Tyquan Thornton’s season-ending ankle injury and Rice’s absence in multiple contests further complicated the passing game. Kansas City finally steadied itself in Week 9, dismantling the New York Jets. The victory improved the Chiefs to 6-2 and kept them firmly in control of the AFC West race. Now, Downs’ arrival gives Mahomes another reliable option as Kansas City looks to regain its offensive explosiveness. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ultimate rhythm valve The biggest fantasy football beneficiary of this transaction is undoubtedly Mahomes. The Chiefs quarterback has continued to produce. However, injuries and inconsistency have occasionally limited the offense’s ability to sustain explosive passing drives. Downs offers a different kind of weapon. He is a quick, technically polished route runner who can consistently uncover underneath and in the intermediate areas. Downs arrives from Indianapolis with 33 receptions for 354 yards and one touchdown through nine games. He can also create separation against man coverage and find open windows against zone defenses. Those traits should appeal to Mahomes. Downs can operate from the slot and provide a dependable outlet. From a fantasy football perspective, this addition could raise Mahomes’ weekly ceiling. Downs gives him another receiver capable of turning short completions into meaningful gains. However, managers should not automatically project Mahomes as a top-five quarterback every week. Kansas City’s offense remains heavily influenced by Walker’s rushing production. Downs will also need time to absorb the playbook. Still, the acquisition gives Mahomes another way to attack defenses. That makes him an appealing starting option throughout the fantasy football playoffs. WR3 with WR2

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Ultimate rhythm valve The biggest fantasy football beneficiary of this transaction is undoubtedly Mahomes. The Chiefs quarterback has continued to produce. Downs gives him another receiver capable of turning short completions into meaningful gains. However, managers should not automatically project Mahomes as a top-five quarterback every week. Kansas City’s offense remains heavily influenced by Walker’s rushing production. Downs will also need time to absorb the playbook. Still, the acquisition gives Mahomes another way to attack defenses. That makes him an appealing starting option throughout the fantasy football playoffs. WR3 with WR2 upside Downs himself is the most interesting fantasy addition. His 33 catches and 354 receiving yards with Indianapolis provide a useful baseline. However, his move to Kansas City could create opportunities for greater consistency. He is joining an offense led by one of the league’s most accomplished quarterbacks. Reid’s system has also historically created opportunities for receivers who excel in space. In full-point and half-point PPR formats, Downs should immediately enter the weekly WR3 conversation, with legitimate WR2 upside. His ability to win quickly from the slot makes him particularly valuable on third downs. His route-running instincts should help him earn targets even when defenses prioritize covering Rice and Kelce. The biggest adjustment will be learning the Chiefs’ terminology and developing timing with Mahomes. Fantasy football managers should therefore exercise some patience during his first appearance. Nevertheless, Downs is a worthwhile waiver-wire priority or trade target. Changing target hierarchy The arrival of Downs creates a fascinating ripple effect across Kansas City’s existing target tree . Rice remains the team’s primary receiving option. He should continue commanding significant volume when healthy. Downs’ presence could actually help him by preventing defenses from concentrating coverage exclusively on the middle of the field. Kelce could also benefit. Downs’ ability to occupy linebackers may create additional space for the veteran tight end. Kelce’s fantasy value remains tied to his established connection with Mahomes, though. Still, having another dependable route runner should make Kansas City’s passing attack more difficult to defend. Worthy’s situation is more complicated. He recently sustained a hamstring injury against the Jets. Downs’ arrival gives the Chiefs additional flexibility while Worthy recovers. Once healthy, Worthy’s vertical speed should complement Downs’ underneath separation. Walker, meanwhile, should remain a central fantasy asset. His three-touchdown performance against New York reinforced how committed Kansas City is to its ground game. Buy into the Chiefs’ passing game The Downs trade is a positive development for Kansas City’s fantasy football outlook. Mahomes gains another reliable target. Downs becomes an intriguing weekly flex option. Rice and Kelce could benefit from more favorable coverage. There will be an adjustment period, but the potential payoff is significant. Fantasy managers should monitor Downs closely as he settles into Reid’s system. If the chemistry develops quickly, Kansas City’s newest receiver could become one of the most valuable midseason additions of the 2026 fantasy football campaign. item.title: AI has made it ‘close to impossible’ to assess university coursework, regulator says
item.description: Office for Students says institutions in England should return to traditional exams and in-person presentations Universities should go back to traditional exams and in-person presentations to grade students after lecturers complained that AI has made it “close to impossible” to assess coursework, according to an investigation by England’s higher education regulator. The Office for Students (OfS) said the credibility of degrees from England’s universities was under threat from the prolific use of AI in essays, dissertations and “open book” exams, with students reporting that their peers boasted of using AI undetected by staff. item.description: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has called for continuous vigilance from the public as Nigeria expects clearance from the World Health Organization (WHO) on Ebola spread in the country. The NCDC Director-General, Dr Jide Idris, called for nationwide alert on Tuesday as he gave an update after the country confirmed an imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease in a traveller from Uganda recently. According to him, although there are no reported new cases in the country, it is not over, as there are still 28 contacts being monitored before the WHO can give Nigeria a clean bill of health on the Ebola virus. The development was after Idris, on Tuesday, noted that 34 of the 62 contacts identified in connection with the case had completed their individual 21-day monitoring period as of November 9, while the remaining 28 were still under follow-up. He said the agency was sustaining contact tracing, investigation of reported alerts, laboratory testing and surveillance at points of entry in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the FCT Administration, state authorities and development partners. Idris cautioned against interpreting the 21 days since the first case was confirmed as the monitoring period for all identified contacts, explaining that each person has a separate 21-day follow-up period. “It’s remaining 28, and not all of them will go at once. So, although they have done 21 days in exclusion, they are still there. “Because they have left the quarantine does not mean we are Ebola-free. We can only be declared Ebola-free after another 21 days again. And it is not by ourselves to declare ourselves Ebola-free. We are still not Ebola-free. “Our surveillance system and contact tracing is throughout Nigeria. Some people manage the airport, other people manage the land borders. item.dc:creator: OpeOluwani Akintayo
item.content:encoded: The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) has called for continuous vigilance from the public as Nigeria expects clearance from the World Health Organization (WHO) on Ebola spread in the country. The NCDC Director-General, Dr Jide Idris, called for nationwide alert on Tuesday as he gave an update after the country confirmed an imported case of Bundibugyo Virus Disease in a traveller from Uganda recently. According to him, although there are no reported new cases in the country, it is not over, as there are still 28 contacts being monitored before the WHO can give Nigeria a clean bill of health on the Ebola virus. The development was after Idris, on Tuesday, noted that 34 of the 62 contacts identified in connection with the case had completed their individual 21-day monitoring period as of November 9, while the remaining 28 were still under follow-up. He said the agency was sustaining contact tracing, investigation of reported alerts, laboratory testing and surveillance at points of entry in collaboration with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare, the FCT Administration, state authorities and development partners. Idris cautioned against interpreting the 21 days since the first case was confirmed as the monitoring period for all identified contacts, explaining that each person has a separate 21-day follow-up period. “It’s remaining 28, and not all of them will go at once. So, although they have done 21 days in exclusion, they are still there. “Because they have left the quarantine does not mean we are Ebola-free. We can only be declared Ebola-free after another 21 days again. And it is not by ourselves to declare ourselves Ebola-free. WHO must be involved. “So as at now, although we don’t have any new case, we still have to be vigilant. We are still not Ebola-free. “Our surveillance system and contact tracing is throughout Nigeria. Some people manage the airport, other people manage the land borders. And you will recollect that we had alerts from Adamawa State and Rivers State. I think the last one was in Borno state that came through the borders. They all turned negative”, he said. This combo photo shows NCDC officials on duty in Nigeria, and response team members helping to wear protective suits before burying a person suspected of having died from Ebola in Bunia, in the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, on May 25, 2026. (Channels TV/GLODY MURHABAZI / AFP) He also stressed that being identified as a contact does not mean that a person has contracted Ebola. The monitoring is intended to ensure that anyone who develops symptoms is identified early and receives an appropriate response. The NCDC urged healthcare workers in public and private facilities to remain vigilant, establish patients’ travel and exposure histories, observe infection prevention measures and promptly report suspected cases to public health authorities. It advised anyone who develops symptoms after possible exposure to Ebola to avoid contact with others and call its toll-free line, 6232, for guidance before travelling to a health facility. Beyond the Ebola response, the agency raised concerns over other infectious diseases, including dengue fever, chikungunya, diphtheria, cerebrospinal meningitis and Lassa fever. It confirmed dengue fever cases in Sokoto and Zamfara states, as well as chikungunya in Sokoto State. To support the affected states, the NCDC said it had deployed national rapid response teams, including entomologists from the National Arbovirus Research Centre in Enugu. The teams are assisting with case identification, laboratory investigations, clinical preparedness, community engagement and mosquito control. This combo photo shows an air ambulance used to evacuate Nigeria’s index Ebola patient on October 26, 2026, and Health Minister Pate. Idris warned Nigerians against assuming that every fever is malaria, noting that dengue and chikungunya could also cause fever, headaches, body pains and joint pains. He said severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding and difficulty breathing could be warning signs of serious dengue complications and require urgent medical attention. The agency also called on states in the meningitis belt to strengthen surveillance, diagnostic services, clinical preparedness and vaccination responses as the dry season advances. On diphtheria, the NCDC said the disease remained a serious concern, particularly among children who had missed routine immunisation. It urged parents and caregivers to check their children’s vaccination status and seek guidance on missed doses. The post Although No New Case, Nigeria Is Still Not Ebola-Free, NCDC Warns appeared first on Channels Television .

item.title: Disney's Legendary 218-Episode Sci-Fi Series Is the Perfect Anti-'Lanterns' Binge
item.description: The fate of Lanterns season 2, and the DC Universe in general, has never been murkier. With the sudden ousting of DC Studios' co-CEOs James Gunn and Peter Safran, the status of HBO's hit show series about two mismatched Green Lanterns who get paired together to solve an intergalactic mystery is up in the air like never before. Season 1 was a critical hit that captured the zeitgeist, and Lanterns co-creator Chris Mundy had already assembled a season 2 writers' room. But in a recent interview , Mundy said the odds of the series continuing were likely "50/50.”

item.title: Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity — UNHCR
item.description: By Ibrahim Hassan-Wuyo Nearly 64,000 Nigerians have fled their homes and crossed into neighbouring Niger Republic since the beginning of 2026 to escape escalating violence involving Islamist militants and armed criminal gangs, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) has said. The UN refugee agency, in a briefing issued on Tuesday, November 10, 2026, warned that the influx was worsening an already difficult humanitarian situation in Niger, which hosts more than 500,000 refugees and asylum-seekers. According to the agency, approximately 327,500 Nigerians are already seeking refuge in Niger, while several hundred others have reportedly crossed into neighbouring Benin Republic because of deteriorating security conditions in northern Nigeria. UNHCR’s Director of External Relations, Dominique Hyde, said most of the newly arrived Nigerians had settled in the border regions of Diffa, in southeastern Niger, and Tahoua, in the western part of the country. The agency disclosed that about 1,200 Nigerians crossed into Diffa in October, while another 3,400 arrived in Tahoua during the same period. It added that more than 23,000 people, over two-thirds of them children, had arrived in Diffa since the beginning of the year. UNHCR expressed concern over the harsh living conditions confronting displaced families, many of whom are staying in makeshift shelters without adequate food, clean drinking water, healthcare and other essential services. Some women, it said, were forced to walk several kilometres daily to fetch water for their families, while humanitarian organisations had reported rising cases of malnutrition, respiratory infections and poor sanitation among the new arrivals. The agency also raised concerns over the registration of displaced Nigerians, disclosing that only about five per cent of those who arrived in Niger this year had been formally registered. It warned that the lack of proper documentation was making it difficult for thousands of refugees to access humanitarian assistance and essential public services. The humanitarian crisis, according to UNHCR, is further compounded by insecurity and climate-related challenges in Niger, particularly in Diffa, where more than 70 per cent of the country’s reported security incidents this year have occurred. Despite the growing pressure, the agency acknowledged the support of Niger’s authorities and host communities, including the provision of land for temporary shelters. However, it appealed for increased international assistance, seeking $11.4 million to expand its humanitarian response in Niger, Nigeria and Benin. The appeal includes $2 million for urgent interventions covering food, water, shelter, healthcare, refugee registration and protection. UNHCR warned that without additional funding, thousands of vulnerable families fleeing violence could be left without access to essential humanitarian assistance. The post Nearly 64,000 Nigerians flee to Niger over insecurity — UNHCR appeared

item.title: NERC approves N30bn for free meters, targets May 2027
item.description: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved N30 billion for the third tranche of the Meter Acquisition Fund (MAF), targeting the provision of free electricity meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerated metering of Band B customers. The Commission announced the approval in Order No. NERC/2026/121 on the operationalisation of Tranche C of the MAF, which took effect on November 2, 2026. Under the arrangement, the N30 billion will be allocated among the 11 electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. NERC said the third tranche was designed to accelerate efforts to close Nigeria’s metering gap, with equitable distribution of meters across states within the respective DisCo franchise areas. The Commission directed the DisCos to conduct transparent procurement processes involving eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stocks. It said maximum procurement prices had been set based on the median national MAP online bid prices recorded during the September 2026 bid cycle. The order provides for payment to selected meter providers in two stages: 70 per cent upon verification of meter stock delivery and the remaining 30 per cent after confirmation of complete installation. NERC emphasised that all meters supplied and installed under the MAF programme must be provided to customers free of charge. It also directed that each meter must prominently display the name of the relevant DisCo, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription, “NOT FOR SALE”. The Commission further stipulated that where a DisCo initiates the relocation of an existing customer’s connection point for revenue protection purposes, the cost must be borne by the distribution company. It warned that sanctions would apply where defaults by DisCos impede or delay meter installation. To ensure transparency and accountability, the order also establishes monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements for the Fund Manager, DisCos and participating meter providers. All supply and installation contracts under Tranche C are required to be filed with the Commission, while the installation of all meters under the tranche must be completed on or before May 31, 2027. NERC urged electricity distribution companies and other stakeholders to comply strictly with the order, describing the initiative as part of efforts to close the national metering gap, strengthen revenue assurance, improve service delivery and protect electricity consumers. The post NERC approves N30bn for free meters, targets May 2027 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Anambra to prioritise erosion control in environmentally responsible communities
item.description: By Vincent Ujumadu The Anambra State Government has resolved to prioritise communities that demonstrate environmental responsibility in its interventions to control erosion across the state. The decision was taken at the weekly State Executive Council (EXCO) meeting in Awka, where the government said communities engaging in practices that worsen erosion would no longer receive priority attention. The prohibited practices include sand excavation, indiscriminate felling of trees, deforestation, dumping of refuse in drainage channels and directing stormwater onto roads. The State Commissioner for Information and Value Reformation, Dr Law Mefor, who disclosed this after the meeting, said perpetrators of such practices would also be prosecuted to serve as a deterrent to others. Anambra has more than 1,000 active erosion sites affecting communities across the state, with experts arguing that addressing the scale of the problem would require federal and international intervention. Also at the meeting, the EXCO directed that Ogbodi in Amichi community, Nnewi South Local Government Area, which was recently cut off by gully erosion, should be reconnected within two weeks through palliative measures. Mefor said the process of identifying a permanent solution to the erosion problem would commence immediately. The erosion had cut off Ogbodi residents from other parts of Amichi, disrupting access and movement within the community. Meanwhile, the State EXCO approved what it described as the “Soludozie Anambra Framework”, an organised and inclusive platform designed to promote development through the Public-Private-Community Partnership (PPCP) model. According to Mefor, the initiative is intended to provide a structured channel through which Anambra indigenes at home and in the diaspora, as well as other well-meaning individuals, can partner with the state government to drive development. He explained that under the framework, the government’s role would generally be limited to documentation, recognition and support where requested, while donors and partners would directly manage their funds and projects. Mefor said the initiative was aimed at positioning Anambra as a model of collective governance and inclusive development, while accelerating the state’s development. The post Anambra to prioritise erosion control in environmentally responsible communities appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Keyamo Flags Off Kogi International Airport Construction
item.description: The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo (SAN), on Tuesday joined the Governor of Kogi State, Ahmed Ododo, to officially flag off the construction of the Kogi International Airport at Zariagi, declaring that the landmark project will place the state on the global aviation map and open up new frontiers of economic opportunities. A statement by Tunde Moshood, Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, noted that Keyamo, who was accompanied by the NCAA’s Director of Public Affairs and Consumer Protection, Michael Achimugu, and other top aides, participated in the historic ceremony alongside the Governor, members of the State Executive Council, traditional rulers, other dignitaries and the immediate past Deputy Governor of Kogi State, Edward David Onoja. Keyamo Flags Off Kogi International Airport Construction on Tuesday, November 10, 2026. Speaking at the event, Governor Ododo described the airport project as a strategic investment in the economic future of Kogi State, emphasising its potential to unlock the state’s enormous agricultural and solid mineral resources for local and international markets. The Governor noted that Kogi State possesses immense economic potential which, if properly harnessed, could position it as a major contributor to Nigeria’s export economy. He explained that the airport would provide a significant boost to the transportation of agricultural produce and mineral resources, attract investors, stimulate commercial activities and create employment opportunities for the people of the state. He further highlighted the airport’s capacity to facilitate the movement of people and goods, strengthen connectivity, attract new businesses and accelerate the development of supporting infrastructure across the state. In his remarks, Keyamo described the flag-off as a historic milestone whose significance would endure for generations. “What is happening here today, what the Governor has done today, will resonate many, many years, centuries after today, 500 years from today. Do you understand the significance of what is happening here today? Let me tell you the significance. Today, as from today, this village called Zariagi will be on the Global Aviation Map,” the Minister declared. He explained that every recognised airport around the world is identified through a global aviation coding system, noting that the establishment of the airport would give Zariagi international visibility within the aviation community through the relevant identification and coding processes of the International Air Transport Association (IATA). According to him, the project represents a significant step in putting Kogi State on the global aviation landscape and connecting it to the wider world. The Minister attributed the possibility of the project to the combination of the economic policies of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Ododo’s vision and determination to translate available resources into meaningful dev

According to him, the project represents a significant step in putting Kogi State on the global aviation landscape and connecting it to the wider world. The Minister attributed the possibility of the project to the combination of the economic policies of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and Governor Ododo’s vision and determination to translate available resources into meaningful development. He maintained that the Federal Government’s economic reforms, particularly the removal of fuel subsidy and the unification of the foreign exchange market, have increased allocations accruing to subnational governments, thereby providing states with greater fiscal capacity to undertake critical infrastructure projects. Keyamo noted that increased revenue alone was not sufficient to guarantee development, stressing that purposeful leadership and the ability to identify and invest in strategic projects were equally important. “However, it takes two to tango. One, the positive policies of President Bola Ahmed Tinubu and the vision of the Governor. These are the two things that combined to make this thing possible today,” he said. Addressing critics who have questioned the rationale behind establishing an international airport in Kogi State, the Minister argued that infrastructure development must sometimes precede the arrival of major investors and commercial establishments. He explained that waiting for international companies, luxury hotels and other major businesses to establish their presence before building an airport would amount to putting the cart before the horse. According to him, an airport is not merely a response to existing economic activities but a strategic catalyst capable of attracting those activities in the first place. “If you are waiting for the best international companies to be here, the best international hotels to be here before you put an airport, you wait for the next one million years, it will not come. It is the airport that attracts these developments. The airport is the precursor. The airport is the forerunner. The airport is the indicator of development,” Keyamo stated. He added that the Kogi International Airport would provide the foundation for increased investment, improved accessibility and the emergence of new economic opportunities that could transform the state in the years ahead. The Minister’s remarks also highlighted the importance of aviation infrastructure in connecting resource-rich communities to markets, investors and international trade networks. Kogi State is endowed with substantial solid mineral deposits, including iron ore, limestone, coal, marble, dolomite, feldspar, kaolin, gypsum, talc and other commercially valuable minerals. The state’s agricultural potential, particularly in the production of crops such as cassava, rice, maize, cashew and palm oil, further strengthens its prospects for expanded trade and export-oriented economic activities. With improved air connectivity, the state stands to benefit from enhanced movement of investors, business executives, technical experts and tourists, while the airport could support the development of cargo logistics and other aviation-related services, subject to the facilities and operational capacity provided. Following his address, the Honourable Minister joined Governor Ododo in performing the foundation-laying ceremony, formally signalling the commencement of the airport project. The flag-off marks another significant step in the Kogi State Government’s infrastructure development drive and its ambition to leverage aviation as an instrument of economic diversification, investment attraction and sustainable prosperity. The Minister commended Governor Ododo for his foresight and commitment to positioning Kogi State for greater economic relevance, expressing optimism that the project would deliver lasting benefits to present and future generations. item.title: Bone broth, sweets ban and acupuncture: Harry Kane’s road to record England cap
item.description: Obsessive attention to detail is helping striker to reach new heights – and a 126th international appearance on Thursday It was Harry Kane’s dirty little secret. Something the England captain got up to after matches. He felt he deserved the indulgence. Yes, it can be revealed, Kane loved to reward himself after a gruelling 90 minutes with a bag of sweets. “I do like a Haribo,” he said with a smile after the Nations League win against Czechia in Prague at the end of September. No more. At the beginning of last season, Kane took the decision to cut out the naughty treats. After a while, he noticed a difference. He felt sharper; able to sprint more, make a greater number of accelerations. Was it down to this latest entry on the list of personal sacrifices? Or was it a consequence of his broader health regime, the scope of which is mind-blowing? Continue reading...
