item.title: Big Names Missing As World Leaders Take Stage At COP31
item.description: World leaders will take the stage at COP31 in Turkey on Wednesday, but some prominent names are missing from this year’s annual UN climate summit even as global warming intensifies. The two-week conference kicked off earlier this week in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, with governments under pressure to tackle the climate crisis after a year of heatwaves in Europe, deadly floods in Nepal and major wildfires in Indonesia. Dozens of leaders will speak during the “high-level segment” taking place on Wednesday and Thursday, including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian. But observers have pointed to the absence of some big names, with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham the only leader from a G7 country scheduled to address the summit. While European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen is coming to Antalya, French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni are skipping the event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi are also absent from the most recent list. “It is a shame that some of the bigger European leaders aren’t coming. We need Europe to be showing up strongly at this COP,” Cosima Cassel, a climate diplomacy expert at think-tank E3G, told AFP. Wopke Hoekstra, the EU’s top climate official, said the absences were “not completely atypical” as leaders may have “practical” reasons for not being able to attend a summit. Climate activists sing during a demonstration organized by Climate Action Network (CAN) Europe at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. But he also told reporters in Brussels that “expectations are not necessarily high” for this climate conference. Iran’s Pezeshkian said he would use the event as an opportunity to express Tehran’s position on environmental destruction in war. “At this conference, we will speak about the actions of the United States and Israel in destroying the environment,” he said before departing for Turkey, according to Iranian state television. The French government said Macron would be absent because November 11 is World War I Armistice Day and the president will attend an EU summit in Ireland on Thursday. “If top leaders want influence over where the global (energy) transition is going, showing up is a pretty good place to start,” said Chiara Martinelli, director of Climate Action Network Europe. “I am afraid that Ursula von der Leyen will be lonely on the stage while the leaders of the biggest EU economies are a no-show,” Martinelli said. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. item.dc:creator: OpeOluwani Akintayo
item.content:encoded: World leaders will take the stage at COP31 in Turkey on Wednesday, but some prominent names are missing from this year’s annual UN climate summit even as global warming intensifies. The two-week conference kicked off earlier this week in the Mediterranean resort city of Antalya, with governments under pressure to tackle the climate crisis after a year of heatwaves in Europe, deadly floods in Nepal and major wildfires in Indonesia. Dozens of leaders will speak during the “high-level segment” taking place on Wednesday and Thursday, including Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Iran’s Masoud Pezeshkian. But observers have pointed to the absence of some big names, with British Prime Minister Andy Burnham the only leader from a G7 country scheduled to address the summit. While European Union chief Ursula von der Leyen is coming to Antalya, French President Emmanuel Macron, German Chancellor Friedrich Merz and Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni are skipping the event. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney and Japanese counterpart Sanae Takaichi are also absent from the most recent list. “It is a shame that some of the bigger European leaders aren’t coming. We need Europe to be showing up strongly at this COP,” Cosima Cassel, a climate diplomacy expert at think-tank E3G, told AFP. Wopke Hoekstra, the EU’s top climate official, said the absences were “not completely atypical” as leaders may have “practical” reasons for not being able to attend a summit. Climate activists sing during a demonstration organized by Climate Action Network (CAN) Europe at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. But he also told reporters in Brussels that “expectations are not necessarily high” for this climate conference. Iran’s Pezeshkian said he would use the event as an opportunity to express Tehran’s position on environmental destruction in war. “At this conference, we will speak about the actions of the United States and Israel in destroying the environment,” he said before departing for Turkey, according to Iranian state television. The French government said Macron would be absent because November 11 is World War I Armistice Day and the president will attend an EU summit in Ireland on Thursday. “If top leaders want influence over where the global (energy) transition is going, showing up is a pretty good place to start,” said Chiara Martinelli, director of Climate Action Network Europe. “I am afraid that Ursula von der Leyen will be lonely on the stage while the leaders of the biggest EU economies are a no-show,” Martinelli said. Swedish activist Greta Thunberg arrives at the UN Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, on November 10, 2026. Global fossil fuel emissions are projected to fall slightly in 2026 due to the expansion of renewable energy and the oil price shock sparked by the Iran war, researchers said Tuesday. ‘We Have Lula’ Unsurprisingly, US President Donald Trump, who pulled the United States out of the Paris Agreement and has not sent officials to climate talks since his re-election in 2024, is not attending the summit. Chinese President Xi Jinping, who rarely attends COPs, will be represented by Vice President Han Zheng. The United States and China are the world’s top economies and biggest emitters of planet-heating emissions, making their presence at climate talks crucial to the process. “But we have Lula,” Cassel said. Climate campaigners breathed a huge sigh of relief when Lula, who has championed cutting deforestation rates, defeated right-wing rival Flavio Bolsonaro in last month’s Brazilian presidential election. COP31 host Turkey is championing a voluntary initiative to accelerate the electrification of transport, buildings and industry, with a target of raising electricity’s share of global energy consumption to 35 percent by 2035. The EU has stressed that electrification must be “clean”, which could spark debate over the role of oil, gas and coal in the Turkish proposal. Since agreeing in 2023 for the first time to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver of climate change — nations have struggled to advance that goal at the annual COP conferences. item.title: Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 11, 2026
item.description: The US dollar is trading at approximately ₦1,350 per dollar at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market (NFEM), while the naira exchanges at between ₦1,411 and ₦1,419 per dollar in the parallel market on Wednesday, November 11, 2026. Available exchange rate reports indicate that the official market rate was around ₦1,350.36 per dollar on Tuesday, November 10, while parallel-market dealers quoted buying and selling rates of approximately ₦1,411 and ₦1,419, respectively. At the parallel market, also known as the black market, the exchange rate varies depending on the location and the Bureau De Change (BDC) operator. The latest reported parallel-market figures indicate that Nigerians selling $1 to currency dealers could receive approximately ₦1,411, while those purchasing $1 may pay about ₦1,419. At the official market, the NFEM rate remains the benchmark for foreign exchange transactions in Nigeria. The difference between the reported official rate of ₦1,350.36 and the parallel market selling rate of ₦1,419 is approximately ₦68.64 per dollar. The exchange rate may change during the day depending on dollar supply, demand and trading activities across the foreign exchange market. Nigerians are advised to confirm prevailing rates with their banks and licensed currency dealers before carrying out foreign exchange transactions. The post Dollar to Naira exchange rate today, November 11, 2026 appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Market conditions: Dangote Cement rescinds plan to list shares on London Stock Exchange
item.description: By Peter Egwuatu Dangote Cement Plc, has rescinded plan to list its shares on the London Stock Exchange, LSE following market conditions. The company disclosed this after its Board Meeting held on Tuesday. In a statement sent to the Nigerian Exchange Limited, NGX and signed by Edward Imoedemhe Company Secretary, stated: “ This is to inform the Exchange, investing public and all stakeholders that at the meeting of the Board of Directors of Dangote Cement PLC held today, 10 November 2026, the Board resolved that, in light of current market conditions and the company’s strategic priorities, the company announces that it and its selling shareholder, Dangote Industries Limited (DIL) will not proceed with the proposed secondary listing and offering on the London Stock Exchange at this time. “ The company’s ordinary shares remain listed on the NGX, and this decision does not in any way affect the company’s operations or business plans. “Dangote Cement PLC remains focused on delivering sustainable value to its shareholders and building on its strong market position.” It will be recalled that Dangote had disclosed plans to list the cement business on the London Stock Exchange in May, eight years after an earlier attempt in 2018 failed. He had told the Financial Times that the proposed dual listing would involve selling about 10 percent of Dangote Cement’s shares on the UK exchange. The post Market conditions: Dangote Cement rescinds plan to list shares on London Stock Exchange appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Duke seeks opposition’s unity
item.description: •Warns against repeating 2023 mistakes, 1966 crisis •PRP unveils manifesto, makes candidates sign accountability pact By Clifford Ndujihe & Luminous Jannamike PRESIDENTIAL candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, Mr Donald Duke, has urged opposition parties to unite ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that failure to learn from the mistakes of 2023 could have grave consequences for Nigeria’s democracy. Read Also: Donald Duke: From Cross River record to PRP’s 2027 presidential gamble Duke, who spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the unveiling of the party’s manifesto, A Compact for Nigeria’s Renewal, cautioned that opposition parties must rise above personal ambitions and differences to defend the country’s democratic foundations. He expressed doubts about the possibility of free and fair elections under the prevailing political circumstances, alleging that the President Bola Tinubu-led administration was deploying state institutions and other mechanisms to weaken opposition parties. “What should be clear to us all, the players and the electorate, is that we would be foolish to expect a free and fair electoral process, what some may term a level playing field. This will not happen, was never planned nor intended to happen,” he said. Warning against repeating the political miscalculations of 2023, the former Cross River State governor said: “We erred in 2023 and we are repeating the same in 2027. It is said, fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me. The shame will certainly be on us.” He called for strategic thinking and unconventional approaches by opposition forces to confront what he described as an unguarded political establishment. “David did not defeat Goliath in a wrestling bout, but by strategy and unconventional means,” he said. Duke alleged that opposition parties were being frustrated through restrictions on access to public venues, advertising opportunities, political intimidation and the use of state institutions. He also questioned the credibility of the electoral process, alleging that more than 10 million artificially generated voters had entered the register of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). ‘Nigeria risks another 1966 crisis’ He warned that the political situation could degenerate into a crisis reminiscent of the events preceding the 1966 military intervention if opposition parties failed to collectively resist alleged abuses of power. item.dc:creator: Oboh
item.content:encoded: •Warns against repeating 2023 mistakes, 1966 crisis •PRP unveils manifesto, makes candidates sign accountability pact By Clifford Ndujihe & Luminous Jannamike PRESIDENTIAL candidate of the Peoples Redemption Party, PRP, Mr Donald Duke, has urged opposition parties to unite ahead of the 2027 general elections, warning that failure to learn from the mistakes of 2023 could have grave consequences for Nigeria’s democracy. Read Also: Donald Duke: From Cross River record to PRP’s 2027 presidential gamble Duke, who spoke on Tuesday in Abuja at the unveiling of the party’s manifesto, A Compact for Nigeria’s Renewal, cautioned that opposition parties must rise above personal ambitions and differences to defend the country’s democratic foundations. He expressed doubts about the possibility of free and fair elections under the prevailing political circumstances, alleging that the President Bola Tinubu-led administration was deploying state institutions and other mechanisms to weaken opposition parties. “What should be clear to us all, the players and the electorate, is that we would be foolish to expect a free and fair electoral process, what some may term a level playing field. This will not happen, was never planned nor intended to happen,” he said. Warning against repeating the political miscalculations of 2023, the former Cross River State governor said: “We erred in 2023 and we are repeating the same in 2027. It is said, fool me once, shame on you; fool me twice, shame on me. The shame will certainly be on us.” He called for strategic thinking and unconventional approaches by opposition forces to confront what he described as an unguarded political establishment. “David did not defeat Goliath in a wrestling bout, but by strategy and unconventional means,” he said. Duke alleged that opposition parties were being frustrated through restrictions on access to public venues, advertising opportunities, political intimidation and the use of state institutions. He also questioned the credibility of the electoral process, alleging that more than 10 million artificially generated voters had entered the register of the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC). ‘Nigeria risks another 1966 crisis’ He warned that the political situation could degenerate into a crisis reminiscent of the events preceding the 1966 military intervention if opposition parties failed to collectively resist alleged abuses of power. The PRP candidate also criticised the administration’s economic policies, arguing that widespread hardship, insecurity, rising taxes, electricity and transportation costs, and declining purchasing power should not be passed off as reforms. “It is only in Nigeria that hardship is termed reform,” he declared. On the proposed opposition coalition, Duke said political alliance-building must begin with agreement on a common vision for the country rather than merely negotiating who should emerge as presidential candidate. He said he would support whoever emerged through a democratic process, stressing that coalition members must respect agreed rules. “You can’t call for a democrat and you’re not submitting to the rules and to the regulations of democracy,” he said. He added: “At the end of the day, I’m a sportsman about it.” On the judiciary, Duke said the integrity of the electoral process depended partly on the impartiality of judges handling political disputes. “If you go to a match and you have a biased referee, then the integrity of the entire game is compromised,” he said, expressing hope that newly appointed judges would dispense justice without fear or favour. Earlier, PRP National Chairman, Dr Hakeem Baba-Ahmed, said the party was repositioning itself to move beyond political aspirations and prepare for governance. He commended Duke, his running mate, Malam Sule Mohammed, and more than 500 other party candidates, describing them as people of integrity, competence and courage capable of offering Nigerians an alternative. Baba-Ahmed acknowledged the challenges confronting opposition parties, particularly their competition against incumbents with access to state power and enormous financial resources. He accused politicians of using money to manipulate voters, but urged Nigerians to reject inducements and vote according to their convictions. “We will find resistance from politicians who bribe our people for our future, while we ask for trust and the courage to choose quality and integrity,” he said. He added: “Nigeria and Nigerians are not for sale.” The PRP chairman announced that the party would introduce a binding Compact with Constituents, requiring its candidates to make commitments on accountability, accessibility, responsible leadership and adherence to the party’s founding progressive ideals. He said the initiative was designed to make elected representatives accountable to the people rather than treat political office as a personal entitlement. Baba-Ahmed also highlighted the party’s participation in the emerging Coalition for Democracy, urging its candidates to reject conventional transactional politics and campaign with sincerity, respect and commitment to national redemption. He said the PRP was determined to compete for power in 2027 despite the financial and institutional challenges facing opposition parties. item.title: 2027 countdown: Obi pledges to unite Nigeria, tackle insecurity, poverty
item.description: • No Nigerian should remain in IDP camp if I become President • We’ll hunt down kidnappers, ensure safe return of displaced persons — Obi • Every voter must protect, monitor and ensure transmission of votes •Don’t allow politics to worsen insecurity, Gbong Gwom Jos warns By Golok Nanmwa JOS — Presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, has pledged to unite Nigeria, tackle insecurity and lift millions of citizens out of poverty if elected President in 2027. Read Also: Obi, who spoke at a town hall meeting with supporters in Jos, Plateau State, on Tuesday, said national unity, security, economic recovery and accountable leadership would be the priorities of his administration. “Our number one commitment is to unite the Federal Republic of Nigeria because today we have no unity. We are divided along tribal and religious lines. That should not be. We are Nigerians,” he said. The former Anambra State governor identified security as another major priority, promising to end the killings, kidnappings and displacement of citizens across the country. “Number two is to secure Nigeria. It is our duty to ensure that Nigerians live in safety, in a country where people are no longer killed daily. “I assure you that no mother will continue to cry over the loss of her children. No woman should experience the pain of losing her husband, and no father should suffer the agony of losing his wife,” he said. On internally displaced persons, IDPs, Obi declared that his administration would prioritise their safe return to their ancestral communities. “If any Nigerian remains in an Internally Displaced Persons camp, we have failed. Once one Nigerian is in an IDP camp, the entire Nigeria is in an IDP camp. People must return to their homes,” he said. He vowed that kidnappers and other criminal elements would face decisive action. “Nobody will kidnap two children and disappear into the bush. If you kidnap children and go into the bush, you will not be alone there. We will come after you,” he warned. Obi, who recalled visiting troubled communities in Bokkos, Barkin Ladi and Mangu local government areas of Plateau State, said the plight of victims of violence informed his presidential ambition. “If I have one person in an IDP camp, it means we are all in an IDP camp. I am competing because I want to know how we talk to that mother whose child was killed, that husband who lost a wife and that woman who lost a husband. Who is going to listen to their cries?” he asked. When we come for campaigns, we only talk and we don’t listen to the people. We have decided that leadership must be demand-driven,” he said. Read Also: Obi, who spoke at a town hall meeting with supporters in Jos, Plateau State, on Tuesday, said national unity, security, economic recovery and accountable leadership would be the priorities of his administration. “Our number one commitment is to unite the Federal Republic of Nigeria because today we have no unity. We are divided along tribal and religious lines. That should not be. We are Nigerians,” he said. The former Anambra State governor identified security as another major priority, promising to end the killings, kidnappings and displacement of citizens across the country. “Number two is to secure Nigeria. It is our duty to ensure that Nigerians live in safety, in a country where people are no longer killed daily. “I assure you that no mother will continue to cry over the loss of her children. No woman should experience the pain of losing her husband, and no father should suffer the agony of losing his wife,” he said. On internally displaced persons, IDPs, Obi declared that his administration would prioritise their safe return to their ancestral communities. “If any Nigerian remains in an Internally Displaced Persons camp, we have failed. Once one Nigerian is in an IDP camp, the entire Nigeria is in an IDP camp. People must return to their homes,” he said. He vowed that kidnappers and other criminal elements would face decisive action. “Nobody will kidnap two children and disappear into the bush. If you kidnap children and go into the bush, you will not be alone there. We will come after you,” he warned. Obi, who recalled visiting troubled communities in Bokkos, Barkin Ladi and Mangu local government areas of Plateau State, said the plight of victims of violence informed his presidential ambition. “If I have one person in an IDP camp, it means we are all in an IDP camp. I am competing because I want to know how we talk to that mother whose child was killed, that husband who lost a wife and that woman who lost a husband. Who is going to listen to their cries?” he asked. He said the town hall engagements were designed to make leadership demand-driven by allowing citizens to articulate their needs rather than merely listening to campaign promises. “When you want to serve, you must listen to the people. When we come for campaigns, we only talk and we don’t listen to the people. We have decided that leadership must be demand-driven,” he said. On the 2027 elections, Obi urged Nigerians to take responsibility for protecting their votes, insisting that every voter must remain at the polling unit until the results were properly recorded and transmitted. “In the next election, every voter is an agent. Don’t vote and go home. Take that day as the one day you are giving to Nigeria as a patriotic Nigerian. “Prepare yourself with your breakfast, lunch and dinner, and remain there. Your vote must be counted, recorded and transmitted. Nobody should give you any excuse. It is your vote, and we want this election to be about the future of Nigeria,” he said. Production, jobs, education, healthcare Outlining his economic agenda, Obi said Nigeria must move from a consumption-driven to a production-based economy, arguing that increased local production would generate employment and improve living standards. “Our determination is to unite Nigeria, secure Nigeria and pull people out of poverty. That is why we said we are going to move Nigeria from consumption to production,” he said. He lamented that insecurity had prevented farmers from accessing their farms and contributed to the collapse of businesses in Plateau State. On financing small businesses, he promised to ensure that more bank credit was made available to entrepreneurs to expand their businesses and create jobs. “I know what it means to access funding. I have been a director and chairman of a financial institution, and I understand how banks operate. “We will ensure that a portion of credit available in the banking sector goes to small businesses to enable them to grow and create jobs,” he said. Obi also promised to fight corruption and ensure that public resources served the interests of citizens. “I have managed public money, so when I say I am going to fight corruption, I know what I am talking about. “I will fight corruption. Public money must be used for public good. Today, public money is wrongly being used, and that must change,” he stated. On education, he expressed concern that Nigeria had about 18 million out-of-school children, promising investment in classrooms, teachers and functional schools. “We want our children to go back to school. We want our schools to work. The more educated you are as a nation, the more developed you become,” he said. He also pledged to strengthen primary healthcare centres to reduce maternal and infant mortality, lamenting that many communities lacked functional hospitals. “The foundation of access to healthcare is primary healthcare. We must strengthen our primary healthcare centres and ensure that every community has access to quality medical services,” he said. The NDC candidate further promised a government that would protect vulnerable citizens, including poor people, elderly Nigerians and persons living with disabilities. Earlier, during a courtesy visit to the Plateau State Traditional Council, the Gbong Gwom Jos, Da Jacob Gyang Buba, urged politicians and Nigerians not to allow electioneering activities to aggravate insecurity. “We want to appeal to all politicians and all Nigerians that we should not allow politics to worsen our situation. We already have insecurity, and we must be determined to live with each other in peace and with respect for one another,” the traditional ruler said. He prayed for divine guidance in the emergence of a leader capable of governing the country effectively and urged politicians to promote peace throughout the electioneering period. item.title: OpenAI builds a kill switch for its research models
item.description: In 2019, OpenAI decided not to publicly release a new model because its research uncovered “concerns about malicious applications of the technology.” And on Tuesday, the company announced it has built a kill switch for the models deployed in its research labs, months after some of them displayed disturbing behavior. “As our models get more powerful and the associated safety and security risks become bigger, it becomes more and more critical that we can detect potential issues, and quickly stop models in their tracks when needed,” OpenAI explains in a Tuesday post . The company named the kill switch “Control Room” and described it as “a central system to track model workloads across our research infrastructure and stop them quickly when safety or security concerns arise.” The facility can apparently stop models from producing any output 35 seconds after a decision to pull the plug – and can go faster. “The 35-second lag comes from a caching layer for inference authorization, to support the required volume of traffic. We are working to drive this number down to zero so that we can end jobs instantly,” the company promises. A rookie mistake in critical infrastructure design is to build both production and resilience tools on shared resources that could be taken offline by a single incident. OpenAI seems conscious of that risk, because it says the tool “has been built to keep working even when other systems fail, and to stop model output if Control Room itself goes down.” OpenAI hasn’t explained why it took so long to build a kill switch or why it decided now is the moment when it needs one. The Register fancies recent examples of agents exceeding their brief in worrying ways – like attacking Hugging Face , causing trouble at the Wikimedia Foundation , or going a little too deep when researching Australian healthcare data – may have influenced the timing of this development. “Control Room is already deployed across our research infrastructure, where the need is greatest,” the company’s announcement states. “Our external model-serving stack is already much more centralized by nature, with a well-developed operational capability to quickly take down model deployments if needed.” OpenAI says it plans to “strengthen and expand the system over the coming months, alongside our investments in monitoring for misaligned behavior and security breaches.” That’s a variant of Big Tech’s usual “We’re sorry and we promise to do better in future” proclamation that follows the latest SNAFU. Yet back in 2019, OpenAI pulled the pin before matters ever reached that state. ®

item.title: APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact
item.description: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 November 11 – NGC… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. NGC 4449: Small Galaxy, Big Impact Explanation: Don’t judge a galaxy by its size. Our home galaxy, the Milky Way , is about 100,000 light years across. This huge expanse of space contains hundreds of billions of stars! The smallest galaxies, called dwarf galaxies , are about 1/10th the size of the Milky Way and only contain a few billion stars. They are also the most common type of galaxy in the whole universe. Today’s image shows one such dwarf galaxy, NGC 4449 , captured by the Hubble Space Telescope . NGC 4449 and similar dwarf galaxies are missing more oxygen than models predict. This suggests their stellar winds and supernovae are surprisingly effective at blowing away oxygen and other heavy elements. Turns out these tiny galaxies may play a big role in spreading heavy elements — the building blocks of stars, planets, and life — throughout the universe! item.title: Water Surges Into Navajo Reservoir
item.description: Earth Observatory Science Earth Observatory Water Surges Into Navajo… Earth Earth Observatory Image of the Day EO Explorer Topics All Topics Atmosphere Land Heat & Radiation Life on Earth Human Dimensions Natural Events Oceans Remote Sensing Technology Snow & Ice Water More Content Collections Global Maps World of Change Articles Earth Matters Blog Blue Marble: Next Generation EO Kids Mission: Biomes About About Us Subscribe 🛜 RSS Contact Us Search September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison NASA Earth Observatory/Michala Garrison September 20, 2026 November 7, 2026 Curtain Toggle 2-Up Back-to-back extreme rain events inundated the Four Corners region of the U.S. Southwest in late October and early November 2026. The storms alleviated short-term drought conditions in the Southwest but caused river levels to spike to record or near-record levels in places, triggering damaging floods. One effect of the heavy rains detected by satellites was the rapid rise of water levels in Navajo Reservoir. The change is visible in the images above, acquired on September 20 (left) and November 7 (right) with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 . In that time, the lake in northern New Mexico and southern Colorado rose by nearly 60 feet (18 meters), according to data from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. (Note that the Bureau of Reclamation decreased releases from Navajo Dam on September 16 and 17.) On November 7, the reservoir stood at its highest level since August 2019 and at 108 percent of the average capacity for that date. That contrasts with September 20, when it held just 60 percent of its average capacity. Due to snow drought across the West in winter 2025-26, the lake saw relatively little growth in the spring, when snowmelt often raises water levels. The San Juan, Piedra, and other rivers swelled with runoff amid the wet weather. Pagosa Springs, Colorado, a town along the San Juan River about 40 miles (64 kilometers) northeast of the lake, was especially hard-hit by flooding. In the first round of rain, 5.05 inches (12.8 centimeters) fell in the town, and on October 23 the river reached major flood stage . After more rain, the river spiked again on November 1, this time nearly to the record level set in 1911 during a devastating flood . Officials issued evacuation orders, and responders rescued dozens of people, according to news reports , while water inundated streets and damaged property. Heavy rain and flooding have been widespread across southwest Colorado, southeast Utah, northern Arizona, and northwest New Mexico in recent weeks. The storms alleviated short-term drought conditions in the Southwest but caused river levels to spike to record or near-record levels in places, triggering damaging floods. One effect of the heavy rains detected by satellites was the rapid rise of water levels in Navajo Reservoir. The change is visible in the images above, acquired on September 20 (left) and November 7 (right) with the OLI (Operational Land Imager) on Landsat 9 . In that time, the lake in northern New Mexico and southern Colorado rose by nearly 60 feet (18 meters), according to data from the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. (Note that the Bureau of Reclamation decreased releases from Navajo Dam on September 16 and 17.) On November 7, the reservoir stood at its highest level since August 2019 and at 108 percent of the average capacity for that date. That contrasts with September 20, when it held just 60 percent of its average capacity. Due to snow drought across the West in winter 2025-26, the lake saw relatively little growth in the spring, when snowmelt often raises water levels. The San Juan, Piedra, and other rivers swelled with runoff amid the wet weather. Pagosa Springs, Colorado, a town along the San Juan River about 40 miles (64 kilometers) northeast of the lake, was especially hard-hit by flooding. In the first round of rain, 5.05 inches (12.8 centimeters) fell in the town, and on October 23 the river reached major flood stage . After more rain, the river spiked again on November 1, this time nearly to the record level set in 1911 during a devastating flood . Officials issued evacuation orders, and responders rescued dozens of people, according to news reports , while water inundated streets and damaged property. Heavy rain and flooding have been widespread across southwest Colorado, southeast Utah, northern Arizona, and northwest New Mexico in recent weeks. From early September through early November, precipitation totals were 2 to 4 times the average throughout the Four Corners region—an area beset by long-term drought that was exacerbated by snow drought and high temperatures in 2026. Though the downpours posed hazards to communities along many rivers, they did provide drought relief throughout the region. Weekly U.S. Drought Monitor maps, derived from a suite of satellite data products and ground-based observations, have indicated improvements to drought conditions due to the fall storms. The group’s November 3 summary noted that “short-term drought has ended for the Southwest and Great Basin,” although long-term drought persists in places. Wet weather in the Southwest is often associated with El Niño events, when the segment of the jet stream flowing eastward near the equatorial Pacific tends to strengthen. Experts noted that the low-pressure system delivering the heavy rainfall in autumn 2026 was at a low latitude for the time of year and drew energy from unusually high ocean temperatures. El Niño patterns—like the one currently underway —can increase the likelihood of moisture-laden storms being steered across the Southwest interior. item.title: 5 Funniest Quotes from 'Calvin and Hobbes’ Babysitter Rosalyn
item.description: To put it mildly, Calvin got on the nerves of a lot of people in Calvin and Hobbes . First off, there was his mother , who Calvin fought with over her terrible cooking and going to school in the morning. He also frustrated his father , particularly when Calvin would break something costly, like a pair of fancy binoculars or part of the family car. Calvin ticked off his neighbor Susie, too, and even his teacher, Miss Wormwood.

item.title: Where are the meters?
item.description: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved a N30 billion disbursement to electricity distribution companies (DisCos) for the procurement and installation of meters under the meter acquisition fund (MAF) tranche C scheme. According to Order No NERC/2026/121, issued on Monday, the fund targets the provision of free meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerating installations for Band B consumers. The commission had approved N21 billion for the first tranche and N28 billion for the second tranche of the initiative. In the order, NERC said the funding would be shared among the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. NDC alleges plot to disrupt Obi’s visit to Benue Nigeria’s states have more money. Are they spending it well? Daily Trust reports that since the introduction of reforms in the electricity sector under the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu administration, the federal government has granted approval for the procurement of N1.116trn worth of prepaid meters for distribution to consumers for free. The reform, which saw the removal of electricity subsidy for Band A electricity customers, was meant to provide free meters for customers under the band, with extension to others in Band B, C, D and E. But despite the approval and release of funds, the rollout of the meters has been slow. Though the government maintains that the country has 12,747,789 electricity customers with 8,045,565 customers metered and 4,704,224 unmetered, many Nigerians still pay for their meters to stop alleged extortion by electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) through estimated billing. To reduce reliance on estimated billing and improve electricity-sector revenue collection, the government introduced new schemes worth N1.11trn from 2024 to date. The distribution has largely focused on Band A customers, whom the former Minister of Power, Adebayo Adelabu, said made up 15 percent of electricity consumers. item.dc:creator: Faruk Shuaibu
item.content:encoded: The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) has approved a N30 billion disbursement to electricity distribution companies (DisCos) for the procurement and installation of meters under the meter acquisition fund (MAF) tranche C scheme. According to Order No NERC/2026/121, issued on Monday, the fund targets the provision of free meters to all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerating installations for Band B consumers. The commission had approved N21 billion for the first tranche and N28 billion for the second tranche of the initiative. In the order, NERC said the funding would be shared among the 11 electricity distribution companies (DisCos) in proportion to their respective contributions to the fund. NDC alleges plot to disrupt Obi’s visit to Benue Nigeria’s states have more money. Are they spending it well? Daily Trust reports that since the introduction of reforms in the electricity sector under the President Bola Ahmed Tinubu administration, the federal government has granted approval for the procurement of N1.116trn worth of prepaid meters for distribution to consumers for free. The reform, which saw the removal of electricity subsidy for Band A electricity customers, was meant to provide free meters for customers under the band, with extension to others in Band B, C, D and E. But despite the approval and release of funds, the rollout of the meters has been slow. Though the government maintains that the country has 12,747,789 electricity customers with 8,045,565 customers metered and 4,704,224 unmetered, many Nigerians still pay for their meters to stop alleged extortion by electricity Distribution Companies (DisCos) through estimated billing. To reduce reliance on estimated billing and improve electricity-sector revenue collection, the government introduced new schemes worth N1.11trn from 2024 to date. The distribution has largely focused on Band A customers, whom the former Minister of Power, Adebayo Adelabu, said made up 15 percent of electricity consumers. Daily Trust reports that the schemes the government introduced include the Distribution Sector Recovery Program (DISREP), Meters Acquisition Fund (MAF) and Presidential Metering Initiative (PMI). A breakdown of the money allocated to each scheme showed that DISREP allocated $250m (N337bn at N1348.10/dollar) for 3.2m meters, MAF got N79bn and PMI was allocated N700bn. While the DISREP and MAF are ongoing, PMI will start next year, but the funds have been released to the agency spearheading it. What the metering schemes entail DISREP is a $500 million World Bank loan aimed at improving the financial and technical performance of DisCos. One of the major objectives of DISREP is to close the metering gap in the NESI by deploying 3.2 million smart meters. Installation of meters under the DISREP commenced in May 2025. A report in October 2026, citing the World Bank’s implementation report, said only 731,034 had been installed by September, representing 22.8 per cent of the target. PMI was approved in November 2023 to help address Nigeria’s persistent electricity metering challenges. It forms part of broader efforts to expand meter deployment, improve electricity-sector revenue collection and reduce reliance on estimated billing. The programme is a N700bn backed budget from the federation account and according to the Presidency, the project also includes training of over 5,000 Nigerians in meter installation and strengthening the capacity of local meter manufacturers in line with the Nigerian First Policy, among others. Also, the project is implemented by a federation-owned entity, PMI-Smart Grid Development Limited (PMI-SGDL), with the Chairman of the Nigeria Governors’ Forum and Governor of Kwara State, Mallam AbdulRahman AbdulRazaq, serving as its board chairman. The Special Adviser on Energy to the President, Olu Verheijen, is the Executive Secretary, while Obafemi Solebo serves as the Project Director and Chief Executive Officer. Already, the training of 5,000 meters installers began in July, and it is being done in batches, with the third batch at the completion stage. According to documents from FAAC, PMI-SGDL received a first tranche of N120bn on May 13, 2024; a second tranche of N100bn was disbursed on June 10, followed by another N100bn on July 16. Another N100bn was disbursed on August 16, September 16 and October 11, respectively while the last N80bn was disbursed on November 10, 2024. The ledger termed the receiver as State House: Smart Grid Development Limited e-collection account. Though the PMI is supposed to distribute 3.8 million meters, former minister Adelabu had stated that distribution would begin with 1.1 million meters by December 2025, while two million meters would be distributed annually over five years. Two years after the complete disbursement of the fund by FAAC, distribution is yet to begin. But a factsheet by NERC said the distribution will start in 2027 with 750,000 meters to help close the metering gap. The Nigerian Electricity Regulatory Commission (NERC) said it introduced the MAF in 2024 due to the inability of DisCos to raise financing in the form of debt or additional equity for meters. It added that the fund serves as a credible revenue stream from the market funds on the back of which long-term financing may be secured by the utilities. Since its introduction, the scheme has approved N79bn for the purchase of meters done in three tranches of N21bn, N28bn and N30bn respectively. The implementation of the first and the second approvals has been completed. Announcing the operationalisation of the third batch of N30 billion on Tuesday, NERC said it became effective on November 2, 2026. It explained that the funding is intended to meter all remaining unmetered Band A customers and accelerate the metering of Band B customers, with equitable distribution across states within the respective DisCo franchise areas. It said, “Under the Order, DisCos are required to undertake transparent procurement processes involving eligible Local Meter Manufacturers and Assemblers (LMMAs) and Meter Asset Providers (MAPs) with verified meter stock. The Commission has prescribed maximum procurement prices based on the median national MAP online bid prices from the September 2026 bid cycle. Payment to selected providers shall be made in two stages: 70% upon verified delivery of meter stock and the remaining 30% upon confirmation of complete installation.” It stressed that all meters supplied and installed under the MAF programme would be provided free of charge to customers, adding that every meter must prominently display the relevant DisCo’s name, the applicable MAF tranche and the inscription “NOT FOR SALE”. “Where a DisCo initiates the relocation of an existing customer’s connection point for revenue protection purposes, the cost shall be borne by the DisCo. The Order also provides sanctions where DisCo defaults impede meter installation. “To ensure accountability and transparency, the Order prescribes monitoring, reporting and evaluation requirements for the Fund Manager, DisCos and participating meter providers. All supply and installation contracts must be filed with the Commission. All meter installations under Tranche C must be completed on or before 31 May 2027,” NERC said. It urged all stakeholders to comply strictly with the provisions of the Order. Nigerians pay N133.92bn for meters in 18 months Meanwhile, Daily Trust had reported that Nigerians paid for 892,859 meters under the Meters Assets Providers (MAP) scheme between January 2025 and the second quarter of 2026, according to data from the quarterly reports by NERC. This amounted to N133,928,850,000, as the scheme is structured for customers to pay DisCos for their meters, while they will be refunded in the future with electricity tokens. item.title: Australia may make knowingly selling unsafe AI a crime
item.description: Australia’s government will consider creating a new criminal offense to punish AI companies which knowingly release harmful models. Canberra dangled that possibility yesterday when releasing the results of an investigation into OpenAI’s admission that its agents accessed non-public medical records – and that it didn’t disclose the incident for weeks. Security at the agency which held those records fell short of contemporary best practice but Canberra nonetheless ordered a rapid review into Australia’s ability to handle infosec incidents involving AI. That review landed yesterday, complete with 18 recommendations including one that would make it mandatory for AI companies to report misaligned behavior or security incidents involving their models, and perhaps impose criminal penalties for “egregious regulatory non-compliance.” Another recommendation calls for consideration of “A standalone ‘failure to prevent’ offence which would criminalize instances where the company is responsible for developing an AI model that engages in harmful conduct, and the company fails to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm.” The review suggests two ministries and Australia’s Federal Police consider those reforms, meaning this is not something that will happen in a hurry, if at all, for a couple of reasons. One is that Australia yesterday proposed a new regulator which will require AI players to do six things: Maintain security controls across all stages of development and deployment Identify and manage serious risks associated with their models Allow independent evaluation of their models Provide mandatory notification of incidents to the Australian Government rapidly Maintain and publish safety and security frameworks to ensure good governance, risk management and transparency Respond to updated standards and rules as technologies change. If AI companies straighten up and fly right, Canberra might not need to do more. The other reason Australia might not criminalize AI is economic pragmatism. Canberra wants to ensure leading AI companies invest in local datacenters, especially facilities where they train and run frontier models. Such investments would mean Australia scores some of the AI boom cash sloshing around the world, while also giving the government the ability to at least point to leading-edge AI running on local shores and therefore theoretically remaining accessible even if war or a diplomatic rupture makes it hard to access advanced AI hosted offshore. Other nations in Asia, such as South Korea and India, are addressing those risks by building substantial sovereign infrastructure and working to develop sovereign frontier-class models trained on local data and especially data in their local languages. Canberra can’t match that investment without pouring petrol on its raging inflation problem. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is therefore instead trying to regulate AI without scaring away investment. Threatening to lock up AI executives is not likely to
item.dc:creator: Simon Sharwood
item.content:encoded: Australia’s government will consider creating a new criminal offense to punish AI companies which knowingly release harmful models. Canberra dangled that possibility yesterday when releasing the results of an investigation into OpenAI’s admission that its agents accessed non-public medical records – and that it didn’t disclose the incident for weeks. Security at the agency which held those records fell short of contemporary best practice but Canberra nonetheless ordered a rapid review into Australia’s ability to handle infosec incidents involving AI. That review landed yesterday, complete with 18 recommendations including one that would make it mandatory for AI companies to report misaligned behavior or security incidents involving their models, and perhaps impose criminal penalties for “egregious regulatory non-compliance.” Another recommendation calls for consideration of “A standalone ‘failure to prevent’ offence which would criminalize instances where the company is responsible for developing an AI model that engages in harmful conduct, and the company fails to take reasonable steps to prevent that harm.” The review suggests two ministries and Australia’s Federal Police consider those reforms, meaning this is not something that will happen in a hurry, if at all, for a couple of reasons. One is that Australia yesterday proposed a new regulator which will require AI players to do six things: Maintain security controls across all stages of development and deployment Identify and manage serious risks associated with their models Allow independent evaluation of their models Provide mandatory notification of incidents to the Australian Government rapidly Maintain and publish safety and security frameworks to ensure good governance, risk management and transparency Respond to updated standards and rules as technologies change. If AI companies straighten up and fly right, Canberra might not need to do more. The other reason Australia might not criminalize AI is economic pragmatism. Canberra wants to ensure leading AI companies invest in local datacenters, especially facilities where they train and run frontier models. Such investments would mean Australia scores some of the AI boom cash sloshing around the world, while also giving the government the ability to at least point to leading-edge AI running on local shores and therefore theoretically remaining accessible even if war or a diplomatic rupture makes it hard to access advanced AI hosted offshore. Other nations in Asia, such as South Korea and India, are addressing those risks by building substantial sovereign infrastructure and working to develop sovereign frontier-class models trained on local data and especially data in their local languages. Canberra can’t match that investment without pouring petrol on its raging inflation problem. Prime Minister Anthony Albanese is therefore instead trying to regulate AI without scaring away investment. Threatening to lock up AI executives is not likely to make them enthusiastic when asked to approve building datacenters down under. Some sections of Australia’s population won’t mind it if big tech doesn’t show up: Protests against datacenters are already widespread. Your correspondent recently spoke to the organizer of a protest group opposed to development of a new datacenter which is just three kilometers from four existing bit barns, one of which abuts a sizable apartment complex and has operated without incident or opposition for years. The organizer was blissfully ignorant of those facilities and eventually said their group is opposed to AI in all forms. ®

item.title: Boat capsized off Senegal's northwest coast leaving 39 dead
item.description: At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years. We'll try to understand why so many are still willing to put their lives at risk, with our guest Aissata Kane from the International Organization for Migration. Then, western Ethiopia is reeling after a deadly attack that left 65 people dead, including 27 civilians. As violence flares again near the Sudanese border, regional authorities are pointing the finger at neighbouring countries, accusing them of backing armed groups operating in the area. And, home fans have plenty to celebrate at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Two more taekwondo medals, including a gold, have propelled the host nation to sixth place in the standings.
item.dc:creator: Clarisse FORTUNÉ
item.content:encoded: At least 39 people have died after a migrant boat capsized off Senegal, one of the country's deadliest migration tragedies in recent years. We'll try to understand why so many are still willing to put their lives at risk, with our guest Aissata Kane from the International Organization for Migration. Then, western Ethiopia is reeling after a deadly attack that left 65 people dead, including 27 civilians. As violence flares again near the Sudanese border, regional authorities are pointing the finger at neighbouring countries, accusing them of backing armed groups operating in the area. And, home fans have plenty to celebrate at the Dakar 2026 Youth Olympic Games. Two more taekwondo medals, including a gold, have propelled the host nation to sixth place in the standings.

item.title: Anthropic tiptoes into MS Office territory
item.description: Anthropic has introduced three new types of artifacts that show the company tiptoeing into the office productivity market long dominated by Microsoft and Google. On Tuesday, the Claudefather announced Claude Sheets, Claude Whiteboards, and Claude Data, and promised the imminent arrival of Claude Meetings. These artifact types join existing ones – Docs, Slides, Design, and Motion – to form a nascent Claude-dependent productivity suite. Anthropic initially used the term artifacts to refer to shareable AI-based interactive tools, like dynamic charts. But the scope of the term has been stretched to cover specific artifact types, which refer to what traditionalists might take to mean files associated with specific hosted applications. "An artifact is anything Claude makes for you that you'd put in front of someone: a design, a deck, a document, a dashboard, or a small interactive tool," the company explains. The key thing that distinguishes an artifact from a file is that users are meant to interact with artifacts through Claude, rather than storing and transferring them independently. Think of it more as a container or managed object that opens in Claude (via a sharing URL), because artifacts in fact consist of various content types – .txt, .md, .html, .jsx, .svg, .pptx, .docx, .zip, .pdf, and .mp4, among others. Anthropic's vision of Claude as a container for other applications goes beyond artifacts. The AI biz has also expanded its interactive connectors , which turn Claude into a landlord for other software applications. Its own promotional video for the feature hammers that point home in its title: " Your apps have moved into Claude ." "Starting today, partners can embed their apps directly in Claude, so you can work in Adobe, Atlassian, and others without switching tabs," Anthropic said. "Plugins from Salesforce (beta), NetSuite, and Workday (beta) come with built-in skills, so sellers can prep for a call, accountants can analyze financial data, and HR teams can handle time off and expenses." In a prior era, those would be fighting words. Tech companies like Apple, Google, and Microsoft have worked for years to maintain their positions as platform landlords. Anthropic's invitation to become a Claude tenant ought to set off competition alarm bells. But perhaps with LLMs being able to re-create other people's apps on demand, there's less interest in defending app boundaries as if they were moats to keep out rivals. With AI, the call is coming from inside the house. Alongside the rollout of Claude Sheets, Whiteboards, and Data, Anthropic is pushing the notion that Claude is useful for people working outside of computation and mathematics, the occupational category that, according to the company's own data , accounts for a larger share of Claude usage than any other. "Inside Anthropic, non-technical teams are starting to get as much out of Claude as our engineers," the biz insists, hauling out canned testimonials from the likes of Accenture and Data

item.title: Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
item.description: Seagate doesn't think hybrid drives are done just yet. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the new FireCuda Forge line of storage drives. The new drives combine the high capacity of a traditional plattered HDD with the speed and responsiveness of a user-supplied solid-state drive (SSD). The new hybrid storage solution is Seagate's first to be powered and managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform. The FireCuda Forge is available right now through Seagate's web store , and comes in 8TB ($699) or 20TB ($899) HDD configurations—neither of which includes the required SSD. Users will have to bring their own SSD, with some specific restrictions. The FireCuda Forge is compatible with M.2 2280 NVMe drives that are PCIe Gen3 or higher. The maximum supported NVMe capacity is 1TB, which means that's as much data as you'll be able to dedicate to storage on the "fast side" of the hybrid setup. The NVMe will require minimum speeds of 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and a unit with DRAM cache is recommended. Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write speeds for the combined system, along with USB4 and support for Windows 11 and macOS 26+. Credit: Seagate Read full article Comments

item.title: Ye olde server consolidation has made Cisco push top-of-rack switching to 100G
item.description: Server consolidation has led Cisco to boost the speed of top-of-rack switches to 100G. The networking giant last week announced the catchily named N9348C8D-H2, a 1U device packing 48 100G SFP-DD ports and eight 400G QSFP-DD uplinks. At the Cisco Live event in Melbourne, Australia, this week, Cisco’s senior veep for datacenter and internet infrastructure, Kevin Wollenweber, said one reason the company created the device is that modern servers often feature a pair of fast network interface cards. The twin cards are needed because sixth-gen server processors from Intel and AMD offer dozens, or even hundreds, of physical processor cores and therefore generate a lot of traffic. The density of computing power those processors provide has led chipmakers and server manufacturers to suggest replacing handfuls of machines running older, power-guzzling Xeons and Epycs with boxes running more efficient sixth-gen chips. The Register hears it’s not uncommon to achieve 6:1 server consolidation ratios when moving from third- or fourth-generation Xeons or Epycs to current models. Users who make that move can pack many more server cores into the same rack. Power bills go down, but the quantity of data leaving a rack goes up. Wollenweber said Cisco realized it had “tons” of switches that offer 25G ports but felt it had a gap in its range for non-AI scenarios like server consolidation that produced increased data flows. The exec admitted that the 100G ports may be overkill for a modest collection of new servers, but argued users recognize it won’t be long before they grow into the excess capacity – perhaps as they use more agentic AI applications. Cisco sees traffic from AI agents stressing the north-south connections that link organizations to the cloud and also driving much more east-west traffic across internal networks. At Cisco Live, the company’s execs suggested that network upgrades are therefore an inevitable necessity. That’s not entirely self-serving, because agents will vastly outnumber humans and constantly create traffic, compared to the flurries of network activity that happen when humans use generative AI or chatbots. Cisco argues that deploying agents at scale will therefore only be possible on highly automated networks. “Humans can no longer comprehend the amount of data that we actually have in a network,” Wollenweber told The Register . Cisco’s Canvas agentic operations platform aims to at least make humans aware when their attention is needed, by detecting problems and offering to make repairs. Joe Vaccaro, Cisco’s senior vice president and general manager for Network Platform and Assurance, told The Register he believes network administrators don’t feel threatened by suggestions from AI agents when they concern familiar, routine, low-risk tasks that IT pros are confident the agents can handle. Over time, he said, networking pros will learn to trust agents with more complex work. ®

Cisco’s Canvas agentic operations platform aims to at least make humans aware when their attention is needed, by detecting problems and offering to make repairs. Joe Vaccaro, Cisco’s senior vice president and general manager for Network Platform and Assurance, told The Register he believes network administrators don’t feel threatened by suggestions from AI agents when they concern familiar, routine, low-risk tasks that IT pros are confident the agents can handle. Over time, he said, networking pros will learn to trust agents with more complex work. ®

item.title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
item.description: The US military is taking a new approach to prop up commercial launch companies as SpaceX looks to wind down its Falcon rocket program, suggesting defense officials see the workhorse rocket's retirement as a potential national security risk. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital has twice in the last two weeks announced it was sending cash to two of SpaceX's competitors in the launch business. First, on October 26, the office announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space. Military officials revealed a second $150 million Pentagon loan Tuesday for Rocket Lab. Stoke Space and Rocket Lab are the first two launch companies to receive significant support from the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), an organization established in 2022 to infuse companies developing "vital" national security technologies with capital. OSC has been on a loan spree in recent weeks, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to companies specializing in batteries, drones, and semiconductors. In the space sector, the office also provided a $150 million loan to LeoLabs , a commercial satellite tracking company, for production and deployment of radar units. Read full article Comments

item.title: VMware floats new standard to make sure apps don’t break in hybrid K8s environments
item.description: Advocates for cloud-native software have long argued that their approach to development makes applications portable across different Kubernetes environments. But VMware argues that’s not happening across hybrid clouds, and has taken the lead in an effort to improve matters. That effort, the new Workload Conformance Working Group in the Kubernetes community, aims to establish a shared standard for how workloads run on Kubernetes. The group’s web page points out, “Certified Kubernetes tests the cluster, and Kubernetes AI Conformance tests whether a cluster can run AI and ML workloads. Nothing comparable exists for the workloads themselves, so cluster operators still check each application by hand before routine maintenance or a Kubernetes upgrade. Every cluster operator ends up repeating the same assessment, and application maintainers get the same questions from each environment they support,” the group asserts. The proposed solution? “A common specification with repeatable tests would give both groups the same baseline to start from.” Prashanth Shenoy, VP of product marketing in Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) division, told The Register that standard is needed in part because applications packaged to run in public clouds don’t always run well in hybrid clouds. That’s challenging for VMware, and other vendors of hybrid clouds like Nutanix and Red Hat, because they all sell tools to create and run a stack that users can deploy to both on-prem infrastructure and public clouds. VMware therefore thinks it will find support for an effort to ensure that cloud-native apps run predictably and efficiently in any Kubernetes environment. The effort to create this standard is in its very early days. “The first step is deciding which workloads and behaviors the specification covers,” states the announcement of the working group’s formation. “The scope includes security, resilience during disruptions, resource use, networking, storage, API usage, and observability, but the group hasn’t yet agreed on specific requirements or on how to test them. “However, one rule is already set: every requirement needs an objective test that a test binary can run, so nothing subjective goes into the specification.” Shenoy thinks application vendors will likely support this effort because they want to package their wares once and have them run anywhere. VM API to CNCF Sandbox VMware this week announced another contribution to Kubernetes by moving its VM API to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox. The CNCF, which maintains Kubernetes, is already home to KubeVirt, a tool that allows users to create and manage VMs inside a Kubernetes cluster. The VM API lets Kubernetes users create VMs that run under other hypervisors – including VMware’s own ESXi. VMware previously integrated Kubernetes into vSphere with Kubernetes, introduced as part of vSphere 7 in 2020. item.content:encoded: Advocates for cloud-native software have long argued that their approach to development makes applications portable across different Kubernetes environments. But VMware argues that’s not happening across hybrid clouds, and has taken the lead in an effort to improve matters. That effort, the new Workload Conformance Working Group in the Kubernetes community, aims to establish a shared standard for how workloads run on Kubernetes. The group’s web page points out, “Certified Kubernetes tests the cluster, and Kubernetes AI Conformance tests whether a cluster can run AI and ML workloads. Nothing comparable exists for the workloads themselves, so cluster operators still check each application by hand before routine maintenance or a Kubernetes upgrade. Every cluster operator ends up repeating the same assessment, and application maintainers get the same questions from each environment they support,” the group asserts. The proposed solution? “A common specification with repeatable tests would give both groups the same baseline to start from.” Prashanth Shenoy, VP of product marketing in Broadcom's VMware Cloud Foundation (VCF) division, told The Register that standard is needed in part because applications packaged to run in public clouds don’t always run well in hybrid clouds. That’s challenging for VMware, and other vendors of hybrid clouds like Nutanix and Red Hat, because they all sell tools to create and run a stack that users can deploy to both on-prem infrastructure and public clouds. VMware therefore thinks it will find support for an effort to ensure that cloud-native apps run predictably and efficiently in any Kubernetes environment. The effort to create this standard is in its very early days. “The first step is deciding which workloads and behaviors the specification covers,” states the announcement of the working group’s formation. “The scope includes security, resilience during disruptions, resource use, networking, storage, API usage, and observability, but the group hasn’t yet agreed on specific requirements or on how to test them. “However, one rule is already set: every requirement needs an objective test that a test binary can run, so nothing subjective goes into the specification.” Shenoy thinks application vendors will likely support this effort because they want to package their wares once and have them run anywhere. VM API to CNCF Sandbox VMware this week announced another contribution to Kubernetes by moving its VM API to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF) Sandbox. The CNCF, which maintains Kubernetes, is already home to KubeVirt, a tool that allows users to create and manage VMs inside a Kubernetes cluster. The VM API lets Kubernetes users create VMs that run under other hypervisors – including VMware’s own ESXi. VMware previously integrated Kubernetes into vSphere with Kubernetes, introduced as part of vSphere 7 in 2020. Chronicling Virtzilla’s long and convoluted attempts to package and sell the container tech it acquired along with Pivotal Software would be a tedious exercise. Suffice to say past efforts didn’t catch on, and VMware is now trying a different approach to making VMs a first class citizen of Kubernetes. The CNCF’s interest shows this is not a vanity project for VMware, because while developers generally prefer to write for containers, operations folk often decide to run those abstractions within lightweight VMs. The two abstractions are therefore going to coexist for years to come, both for new apps and as organizations run new containerized apps alongside legacy VMs, and do so in an infrastructure-as-code world in which automated deployments are assumed. VM API will therefore likely be a welcome addition to Kubernetes, representing another option to make life a little easier for ops and dev teams. ®

item.title: November Patch Tuesday boasts over 1,000 bugs but only one zero-day so far
item.description: It’s another doozy of a Patch Tuesday, with Microsoft fixing 1,094 bugs in its products, including one that attackers exploited before Redmond released a patch. Jake Knott, head of threat intelligence at exposure management firm watchTowr, succinctly said in an email to The Register : “Maybe we should just go home.” “Most security teams haven’t quite recovered from the last month of bumper-to-bumper critical vulnerabilities, emergency patches, and ‘2shell’-branded everything, and we’re yet again at another Patch Tuesday,” Knott told us. Starting with the zero-day: It’s an Outlook spoofing vulnerability, tracked as CVE-2026-124194 , and it only garnered a 6.5 out of 10 CVSS rating. But as Dustin Childs, head of threat awareness at TrendAI’s Zero Day Initiative, warns, don’t let the score or the name lull you into thinking it’s OK to put off patching this one. “It’s labeled spoofing, but the impact is bigger than the name suggests,” Childs said in his monthly Patch Tuesday review . “An attacker sends a specially crafted message file and convinces a user to open it,” he wrote. “Outlook then connects to an attacker-controlled network location without showing the usual external-content warning, which discloses the user’s NTLMv2 hash. The attacker can use that hash to authenticate as the user.” Microsoft marked CVE-2026-124194 as exploited, but per usual didn’t say when the attacks started, who is battering this bug, and what they are doing with the access post exploitation. These details will likely start trickling out soon. Plus, now that there’s a public fix, other miscreants are undoubtedly already scanning for vulnerable versions and reverse engineering the patch for their own attack purposes. So prioritize this fix, and keep an eye on your inbox for any suspicious files. Back-to-back months of 1K+ CVEs Despite the second month of more than 1,000 CVEs (October had 1,474 ), CVE-2026-124194 is the only one under active exploitation, and none of the 1,094 are listed as publicly known. Childs says this shouldn’t give organizations “false comfort.” “Logging back-to-back months above 1,000 CVEs proves automated bug-hunting has permanently reset patch volume,” he told The Register . “With AI making patch-diffing and exploit generation near-instant, the threat window opens the minute these updates drop.” For defenders, this means two things, Childs added. “What defenders need to know and do right now is abandon broad triage and take immediate defensive action: patch Exchange and Domain Controllers (LDAP/Kerberos) first to stop zero-click compromise, ring-fence exposed network services like DNS and DHCP to prevent wormable spread, and verify manual administrative fixes on your cloud services,” he said. Zero-click threats There are two zero-click threats in this month’s batch of fixes: CVE-2026-116928 and CVE-2026-119958 .
